title.zh: 卷二百九十六 列傳第五十五 韓丕 師頏 張茂直 梁顥 楊徽之 呂文仲 王著 呂祐之 潘慎修 杜鎬 查道
title.en: Volume 296 Biographies 55: Han Pi, Shi Hang, Zhang Maozhi, Liang Hao, Yang Huizhi, Lu Wenzhong, Wang Zhe, Lu Youzhi, Pan Shenxiu, Du Gao, Cha Dao
title.raw: 卷二百九十六 列傳第五十五 韓丕 師頏 張茂直 梁顥 楊徽之 呂文仲 王著 呂祐之 潘慎修 杜鎬 查道 Volume 296 Biographies 55: Han Pi, Shi Hang, Zhang Maozhi, Liang Hao, Yang Huizhi, Lu Wenzhong, Wang Zhe, Lu Youzhi, Pan Shenxiu, Du Gao, Cha Dao

sentences.zh: 韓丕，字太簡，華州鄭人。

translations.literal: Han Pi, style name Taejian, was a native of Zheng in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Pi, courtesy name Taejian, was from Zheng in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父杲，晉開運中，為曲陽主簿，契丹攻城，陷沒焉。

translations.literal: His father Gao, during the Kaiyun era of Jin, served as registrar of Quyang; when the Khitans attacked the city, he was captured and lost.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao had been registrar of Quyang in the Kaiyun era of Jin; when the Khitans besieged the city, he was taken captive and never returned.

sentences.zh: 母改適他氏。

translations.literal: His mother remarried into another family.
translations.idiomatic: His mother remarried elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 丕幼孤貧，有志操，讀書於驪山、嵩陽，通《周易》、《禮記》，為人講說。

translations.literal: Pi was orphaned young and poor, yet possessed resolve and integrity; he studied at Lishan and Songyang, mastered the Book of Changes and the Book of Rites, and lectured for others.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from childhood, Pi nevertheless held firm principles. He studied at Lishan and Songyang, mastered the Book of Changes and the Book of Rites, and taught others by lecturing on the classics.

sentences.zh: 常有山林之志，家雖甚貧，處之晏如。

translations.literal: He often harbored the will to dwell in mountains and forests; though his household was very poor, he remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He often yearned for a life in the hills, and though his family was desperately poor, he remained entirely at ease.

sentences.zh: 年長，始學文。

translations.literal: Only when he was older did he begin to study letters.
translations.idiomatic: He did not take up formal literary study until he was already grown.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，鄭牧知文州，與之偕行，遂薄遊兩川。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao era, Zheng Mu governed Wen Prefecture; Pi traveled with him and so made a brief tour of the Two Shu regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaibao era, when Zheng Mu was prefect of Wen, Pi accompanied him on his travels and so made a brief tour through the Two Shu.

sentences.zh: 及牧知成都，劉熙古延置門下，掌書奏，以孫女妻之。

translations.literal: When Mu became prefect of Chengdu, Liu Xigu invited Pi into his household, put him in charge of documents and memorials, and gave him his granddaughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu became prefect of Chengdu, Liu Xigu took Pi into his household to manage documents and memorials, and married him to his granddaughter.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年舉進士，聲名籍甚，公卿多薦之者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination; his fame was very great, and many ministers and nobles recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Taiping Xingguo, and his reputation spread so widely that many high officials recommended him.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《孟母碑》、《返魯頌》，人多諷誦之。

translations.literal: He once composed the Stele of Mencius's Mother and the Ode on Returning to Lu, which many people recited and chanted.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote such works as the Stele of Mencius's Mother and the Ode on Returning to Lu, which many people memorized and recited.

sentences.zh: 解褐大理評事、通判衡州。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office dress he was made an evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent prefect of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he was appointed evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent prefect of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 石熙載薦其文行，代還，以文學試中書，擢著作佐郎、直史館，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Shi Xizai recommended his literary conduct; when his term ended and he returned, he passed the literary examination at the Secretariat and was promoted to assistant compiler and attached to the Historiography Institute, and was granted the crimson fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xizai recommended him for his learning and conduct. When his tour ended and he returned to court, he passed the literary examination at the Secretariat and was promoted to assistant compiler with a concurrent post at the Historiography Institute, and received the crimson fish tally.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改左拾遺。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to the post of Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷職方員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was moved to vice director of the Bureau of Military Appointments and charged with drafting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Appointments and given charge of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，加虞部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was additionally made a director of the Bureau of Parks and Forests.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongxi era he was additionally appointed director of the Bureau of Parks and Forests.

sentences.zh: 二年，與賈黃中、徐鉉同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year he served with Jia Huangzhong and Xu Xuan as co-supervisor of the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served with Jia Huangzhong and Xu Xuan as co-supervisor of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 丕屬思艱澀，及典書命，傷於稽緩。

translations.literal: Pi found composition arduous and labored; when he took charge of edicts, he suffered from slowness and delay.
translations.idiomatic: Pi composed with difficulty, and once he was charged with drafting edicts, his work suffered from excessive slowness.

sentences.zh: 宰相宋琪性褊急，常加督責，或申以諧謔，丕不能平。

translations.literal: The chief minister Song Qi was narrow and impatient by nature and often pressed and reproved him, sometimes expressing it in banter; Pi could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Song Qi was narrow and impatient by nature and often pressed and scolded him, sometimes dressing his rebukes in jest; Pi could not bear it in peace.

sentences.zh: 又舍人王祐以前輩負氣，每陵轢面折之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Attendant Gentleman Wang You, relying on seniority and pride of spirit, often overbore and openly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant Gentleman Wang You, as his senior, was proud and overbearing and often humiliated him with open rebukes.

sentences.zh: 丕乃表求外郡，出知虢州，就改職方郎中。

translations.literal: Pi then memorialized requesting an outer prefecture, went out as prefect of Guo, and on the spot was changed to director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Pi then petitioned for an appointment outside the capital, became prefect of Guo, and at the same time was promoted to director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，拜右諫議大夫，賜金紫，知河陽、濠州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee, granted gold and purple, and made prefect of Heyang and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee, granted gold and purple insignia, and made prefect of Heyang and Hao.

sentences.zh: 丕起寒素，以沖澹自處，不奔競於名宦，太宗甚嘉重之。

translations.literal: Pi rose from humble origins, conducted himself with quiet detachment, did not scramble for fame and office, and Taizong greatly prized and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi came from humble origins, lived with quiet detachment, and never scrambled for rank or office; Taizong greatly prized him for it.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，召入為翰林學士，終以遲鈍不敏於用。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was summoned in as Hanlin academician, but in the end because of slowness and dullness he was not adept in service.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy, but in the end his slowness left him ill suited to court duties.

sentences.zh: 俄罷職，充集賢殿修撰、知均州。

translations.literal: Before long he was removed from office, made compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and prefect of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed and appointed compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Jun.

sentences.zh: 就遷給事中、工部侍郎，徙金州。

translations.literal: He was then moved to Supervising Secretary and vice minister of Works, and transferred to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Supervising Secretary and vice minister of Works, and transferred to Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召還，充史館修撰，又出知滁州，就加禮部。

translations.literal: He was recalled, made compiler at the Historiography Institute, then went out again as prefect of Chu, and on the spot was additionally made vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he served as compiler at the Historiography Institute, then went out again as prefect of Chu and was at the same time promoted to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 丕純厚畏慎，似不能言者。

translations.literal: Pi was pure, thick, fearful, and cautious, as though one who could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was pure-hearted, cautious, and reserved, almost as if he could not speak at all.

sentences.zh: 歷典州郡，雖不優於吏事，能以清介自持，時稱其長者云。

translations.literal: Having governed several prefectures, though he was not superior in administrative affairs, he was able to maintain himself with purity and integrity, and the age called him an elder worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was not especially skilled in administrative affairs during his terms as prefect, he upheld himself with purity and integrity, and his contemporaries praised him as a man of mature virtue.

sentences.zh: 師頏，字霄遠，大名內黃人。

translations.literal: Shi Hang, style name Xiaoyuan, was a native of Neihuang in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hang, courtesy name Xiaoyuan, was from Neihuang in Daming.

sentences.zh: 父均，後唐長興二年進士，終永興節度判官，因家關右。

translations.literal: His father Jun passed the jinshi in the second year of Changxing of Later Tang and ended as military commissioner-assessor of Yongxing; the family therefore settled in the Guanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun passed the jinshi in the second year of Changxing of Later Tang and ended his career as assessor to the military commissioner of Yongxing; the family then settled in the Guanxi region.

sentences.zh: 頏少篤學，與兄頌齊名。

translations.literal: Hang from youth studied earnestly and was equally famed with his elder brother Song.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hang studied with deep devotion and shared equal fame with his elder brother Song.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年舉進士，竇儀典貢舉，擢之上第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he took the jinshi examination; Dou Yi presided over the examinations and raised him to the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi examination in the second year of Jianlong; Dou Yi presided over the examinations and placed him at the top of the list.

sentences.zh: 釋褐耀州軍事推官，以疾解，久不赴調。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office dress he was made investigating clerk for military affairs of Yao Prefecture; he resigned on account of illness and for a long time did not report for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he was appointed investigating clerk for military affairs of Yao Prefecture, but resigned because of illness and for a long time did not report for a new assignment.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，復為解州推官。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao era he again served as investigating clerk of Jie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he again served as investigating clerk of Jie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，召還，遷大理寺丞、陝西河北轉運判官，就改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was recalled, promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and transport-assessor of Shaanxi and Hebei, and on the spot changed to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was recalled, promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and transport-assessor for Shaanxi and Hebei, and at the same time appointed assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，遷監察御史、通判永興軍府。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he was moved to investigating censor and concurrent prefect of the Yongxing military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was promoted to investigating censor and concurrent prefect of the Yongxing military prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐秦王廷美假公帑緡錢，左授乾州團練副使，尋復舊官。

translations.literal: He was implicated because Prince of Qin Tingmei had borrowed public treasury strings of cash; he was demoted to vice commissioner of military training at Qian and soon restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was implicated in Prince of Qin Tingmei's borrowing of public funds, demoted to vice commissioner of military training at Qian, and soon restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，改殿中侍御史、通判邠州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to palace attendant censor and concurrent prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to palace attendant censor and concurrent prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 徙知簡州，轉起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Jian and then made Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Jian and then promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.

sentences.zh: 以公累去官，復為殿中侍御史，知資、眉二州。

translations.literal: Because of public entanglement he left office, then again became palace attendant censor and governed Zi and Mei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office because of public entanglement, he again became palace attendant censor and governed Zi and Mei.

sentences.zh: 頏所至，以簡靜為治，蜀人便之。

translations.literal: Wherever Hang arrived, he governed with simplicity and quiet, and the people of Shu found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, Hang governed with simplicity and restraint, to the great convenience of the people of Shu.

sentences.zh: 代還，遷侍御史、知安州，賜緡錢二十萬。

translations.literal: When his replacement returned he was promoted to attendant censor and made prefect of An, and was granted two hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: When his successor arrived he was promoted to attendant censor and appointed prefect of An, and was granted two hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 移朗州，超拜工部郎中，命知陝州，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was moved to Lang Prefecture, promoted by special order to director of the Ministry of Works, ordered to govern Shan, and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Lang, he was promoted by special order to director of the Ministry of Works, appointed prefect of Shan, and granted gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 時西鄙用兵，餫道所出，軍士多亡命，嘯聚山林為盜。

translations.literal: At the time the western frontier was at war; where the supply routes passed, many soldiers deserted and gathered in the hills and forests as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: War was then raging on the western frontier; along the supply routes many soldiers deserted and banded together in the hills as robbers.

sentences.zh: 頏嚴其巡捕，盜越他境。

translations.literal: Hang made patrol and capture strict, and the bandits crossed into other jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Hang tightened patrols and arrests so severely that the bandits fled into neighboring jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 改刑部郎中，未幾召還。

translations.literal: He was changed to director of the Ministry of Punishments, and before long was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Ministry of Punishments, and before long was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 真宗以其舊人，素負才望，而久次於外，累召對，詢其文章。

translations.literal: Zhenzong, because he was an old acquaintance who had long borne literary reputation yet long remained outside, repeatedly summoned him for audience and inquired about his writings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong knew him as an old acquaintance of long-standing literary reputation who had spent many years in the provinces; he repeatedly summoned Hang for audience and questioned him about his writings.

sentences.zh: 頏謙遜自晦，上益嘉之。

translations.literal: Hang was modest and concealed his talents, and the emperor all the more praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Hang answered with modest reserve, and the emperor prized him all the more.

sentences.zh: 翌日，命以本官知制誥，兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: The next day he was ordered, in his present office, to draft imperial edicts and concurrently to serve as compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was ordered to draft imperial edicts in his present rank and concurrently to serve as compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，與溫仲舒、張詠同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he served with Wen Zhongshu and Zhang Yong as co-supervisor of the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he served with Wen Zhongshu and Zhang Yong as co-supervisor of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: The following year he was summoned into the Hanlin as academician.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as academician.

sentences.zh: 五年，復與陳恕同典貢部，又知審官院、通進銀臺封駁司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again with Chen Shu presided over the examination bureau, and also directed the Bureau for Review of Appointments, the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace Office for Memorial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again presided over the examination bureau with Chen Shu, and also directed the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the offices for transmission and memorial review.

sentences.zh: 俄卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 詔遣官護葬，給其子仲回秘書丞奉終喪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials to escort the funeral, and gave his son Zhonghui the post of secretary director to observe the full mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered officials to escort the funeral and appointed his son Zhonghui secretary director so that he could observe the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 頏曠達夷雅，搢紳多慕其操尚。

translations.literal: Hang was broad-minded, easy, and refined; many gentry admired his conduct and aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: Hang was broad-minded and refined in spirit, and many officials admired his character.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子三人：仲回，端拱元年進士及第，至太常博士；

translations.literal: He had three sons: Zhonghui, who passed the jinshi in the first year of Duangong and rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Zhonghui, who passed the jinshi in the first year of Duangong and rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 仲宰，國子博士；

translations.literal: Zhongzai, erudite of the Directorate of Education;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzai, erudite of the Directorate of Education;

sentences.zh: 仲說，殿中丞。

translations.literal: Zhongshuo, director within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhongshuo, director within the palace.

sentences.zh: 張茂直

translations.literal: Zhang Maozhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhi

sentences.zh: 張茂直，字林宗，兗州瑕丘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Maozhi, style name Linzong, was a native of Xiaqiu in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhi, courtesy name Linzong, was from Xiaqiu in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父延昇，以經術教授鄉里。

translations.literal: His father Yansheng taught the classics in the countryside by the methods of classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yansheng taught the classics in their home district.

sentences.zh: 茂直方弱冠，慕容彥超據州城，驅之守陴。

translations.literal: When Maozhi had just reached manhood, Murong Yanchao held the prefectural city and drove him to defend the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: While Maozhi was still in his early twenties, Murong Yanchao seized the prefectural city and forced him to help defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 及周師破敵，擁城守者列坐，將斬之。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army defeated the enemy, those who had held the city were made to sit in a row and were about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army broke the enemy, the defenders were lined up to be executed.

sentences.zh: 有卒挾刃謂茂直曰：「汝髮甚鬒，惜為頸血所汙，可先斷之。

translations.literal: A soldier seized a blade and said to Maozhi, "Your hair is very black; it would be a pity for neck blood to stain it—you may cut it off first."
translations.idiomatic: A soldier seized a blade and said to Maozhi, "Your hair is very black; it would be a pity for your neck blood to stain it—you may cut it off first."

sentences.zh: 」茂直許焉。

translations.literal: " Maozhi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhi agreed.

sentences.zh: 刃未及髮，會得釋。

translations.literal: The blade had not yet reached his hair when by chance he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The blade had not yet touched his hair when, by chance, he was released.

sentences.zh: 後勵志於學。

translations.literal: Afterward he resolved his will upon study.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he devoted himself wholeheartedly to learning.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，州將器其為人，首薦之，且給錢五萬，以助其裝。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao era the prefectural commander valued his character, was the first to recommend him, and moreover gave fifty thousand cash to help with his traveling expenses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era the prefectural commander admired his character, was the first to recommend him, and gave him fifty thousand cash toward his traveling expenses.

sentences.zh: 二年，登進士第，解褐海州推官，進司農寺丞、通判泰州。

translations.literal: In the second year he passed the jinshi examination, upon leaving office dress became investigating clerk of Hai Prefecture, and was advanced to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries and concurrent prefect of Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as investigating clerk of Hai Prefecture, and was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries and concurrent prefect of Tai.

sentences.zh: 為轉運使韋務昇誣奏，徙監梓州富國監。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner Wei Wusheng falsely memorialized against him, and he was moved to supervise the Fuguo depot of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Wei Wusheng lodged a false accusation against him, and he was transferred to supervise the Fuguo depot at Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代還，自陳得雪。

translations.literal: When his replacement returned he stated his case and was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When his successor arrived he petitioned in his own defense and was cleared of the charge.

sentences.zh: 復通判靜安軍。

translations.literal: He again served as concurrent prefect of the Jing'an army.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as concurrent prefect of the Jing'an army.

sentences.zh: 軍不領縣，城之外，即深州之下博，茂直奏割下博隸焉。

translations.literal: The army did not administer counties; outside the city wall lay Xiabo of Shen Prefecture, and Maozhi memorialized to detach Xiabo and attach it to the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army had no county under its jurisdiction; beyond the city wall lay Xiabo in Shen Prefecture, and Maozhi petitioned to have Xiabo placed under the army's administration.

sentences.zh: 進秩著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 扈蒙薦其才，改秘書丞。

translations.literal: Hu Meng recommended his talent, and he was changed to secretary director.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Meng recommended his talent, and he was appointed secretary director.

sentences.zh: 會福州民訟田，命茂直按之，將行，留不遣。

translations.literal: When the people of Fuzhou were litigating over fields, Maozhi was ordered to investigate; as he was about to depart, he was detained and not sent.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Fuzhou were litigating over land, Maozhi was ordered to investigate; he was about to depart when the court detained him and did not send him.

sentences.zh: 參知政事李至稱其端實，命入益王元傑府為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councilor Li Zhi praised his uprightness and solidity and ordered him into the household of Prince of Yi Yuanjie as recorder-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Li Zhi praised his integrity and had him appointed recorder in the household of Prince of Yi Yuanjie.

sentences.zh: 王好學，多為詩什，遇茂直甚厚。

translations.literal: The prince loved learning and often composed poetry; he treated Maozhi very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loved learning and often wrote poetry; he treated Maozhi with great favor.

sentences.zh: 雖受時果之賜，亦分餉焉。

translations.literal: Though he received seasonal fruit as gifts, he also shared portions with others.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he received seasonal fruit as gifts from the prince, he shared them with others.

sentences.zh: 王嘗遣使徵詩，茂直援筆而就，甚稱賞之。

translations.literal: The prince once sent a messenger to request a poem; Maozhi took up the brush and finished at once, and the prince greatly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once sent a messenger to request a poem; Maozhi took up his brush and finished at once, and the prince greatly admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 茂直淳至寡言，晚年多疾，才思梗澀不稱職。

translations.literal: Maozhi was pure, sincere, and sparing of words; in his later years he had many illnesses, and his literary thought was obstructed and sluggish, so that he did not fit his office.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhi was sincere and sparing of speech; in his later years he suffered frequent illness, and his literary powers grew stiff and sluggish so that he no longer suited his post.

sentences.zh: 改秘書少監，出知潁州。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice director of the Secretariat and went out as prefect of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Xianping, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 子：成列，端拱二年進士及第；

translations.literal: His sons: Chenglie, who passed the jinshi in the second year of Duangong;
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chenglie, who passed the jinshi in the second year of Duangong;

sentences.zh: 成務，比部員外郎。

translations.literal: Chengwu, vice director of the Bureau of Review.
translations.idiomatic: and Chengwu, vice director of the Bureau of Review.

sentences.zh: 梁顥，字太素，鄆州須城人。

translations.literal: Liang Hao, style name Taisu, was a native of Xucheng in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hao, courtesy name Taisu, was from Xucheng in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖涓，成武主簿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Juan was registrar of Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Juan served as registrar of Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 祖惟忠，以明經歷佐使府，至天平軍節度判官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Weizhong, having passed the classics examination, served in successive staff posts of commissionerates, rising to military commissioner-assessor of the Tianping army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Weizhong passed the classics examination and served in successive staff posts of military commissioners, rising to assessor of the Tianping army.

sentences.zh: 父文度早世，顥養於叔父。

translations.literal: His father Wendu died young, and Hao was raised by his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wendu died young, and Hao was raised by his uncle.

sentences.zh: 王禹偁始與鄉貢，顥依以為學，嘗以疑義質於禹偁，禹偁拒之不答。

translations.literal: When Wang Yucheng first presented himself for the provincial examination, Hao relied on him for study; he once submitted doubtful points to Wang Yucheng, and Wang Yucheng refused and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yucheng first sat for the provincial examination, Hao studied under him and once asked Wang about points he found difficult; Wang refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 顥發憤讀書，不期月，復有所質，禹偁大加器賞。

translations.literal: Hao in indignation applied himself to reading; in less than a month he again had points to submit, and Wang Yucheng greatly valued and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Stung to anger, Hao threw himself into his books; in less than a month he returned with new questions, and Wang Yucheng greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士，不中第，留闕下。

translations.literal: When he first took the jinshi examination he did not pass and remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On his first attempt at the jinshi examination he failed and remained at the capital.

sentences.zh: 獻疏曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 「臣歷觀史籍，唐氏之御天下也，列聖間出，人文闡燿，尚且渴於共治，旁求多彥，設科之選，逾四十等。

translations.literal: "Your subject has broadly surveyed the historical records: when the Tang house ruled All Under Heaven, sage after sage appeared in succession and human culture was brilliantly unfolded; they still thirsted for joint governance, sought widely for many worthies, and established examination selections exceeding forty grades."
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject has reviewed the histories: when the Tang ruled the realm, sage emperors arose in succession and culture flourished brilliantly, yet they still yearned for shared governance, sought talent far and wide, and established examination categories numbering more than forty."

sentences.zh: 當時秉筆之士，彬彬翔集，表著所以。

translations.literal: At that time the men who wielded the brush gathered in refined abundance, and their achievements were manifest in the records.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters then gathered in refined abundance, and their achievements were recorded for all to see.

sentences.zh: 左右前後，有忠有良，導化原、樹治本者，享三百年，得人之由也。

translations.literal: Before and behind, to left and right, there were loyal and worthy men who guided transformation at its source and planted governance at its root; they enjoyed three hundred years—this was the reason they obtained men.
translations.idiomatic: On every side were loyal and capable men who guided civilization at its source and planted good governance at its root; the dynasty endured three hundred years because it knew how to win such men.

sentences.zh: 五代不競，茲制日淪。

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties did not strive, and this institution daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties could not compete, and this institution fell further each day.

sentences.zh: 國家興儒，追風三代。

translations.literal: Our state has raised Confucian learning and pursues the wind of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has revived Confucian learning and seeks to follow the example of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 方今科名之設，俊造畢臻，秉筆者如林，趨選者如雲。

translations.literal: Now that examination titles are established, outstanding candidates all arrive; those who wield the brush are like a forest, and those who hurry to selection are like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Today, with examination titles established, outstanding candidates gather from every quarter; men of letters crowd the halls like trees in a forest, and aspirants press toward selection like clouds in the sky.

sentences.zh: 貢於諸侯，考於春官，陛下躬臨慎擇，必盡至公。

translations.literal: They are presented to the feudal lords, examined by the Ministry of Rites, and Your Majesty personally attends and carefully selects, surely exhausting utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates are presented through the provinces, examined by the Ministry of Rites, and Your Majesty personally oversees the careful selection, surely with the utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 奈何所取不出於詩賦、策論，簡於心者援而陟之，咈於心者推而黜之，寧無濫陟枉黜之失耶？

translations.literal: Alas, what is taken does not come from poetry, rhapsodies, policy essays, and discourses; those who please the heart are pulled up and promoted, those who offend the heart are pushed down and dismissed—can there be no error of reckless promotion and wrongful dismissal?
translations.idiomatic: Yet selection rests not on poetry, rhapsodies, policy essays, and discourses alone; those who please the examiner are pulled up, while those who displease him are pushed aside—can there be no error of reckless promotion and wrongful dismissal?

sentences.zh: 其間闒茸妄進，濫廁科場者，間亦有之。

translations.literal: Among them there are also at times the lowly and incompetent who advance rashly and crowd into the examination hall without warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, too, are at times unworthy men who advance rashly and crowd into the examination hall without warrant.

sentences.zh: 若曰陛下嘉惠孤寒沉滯之士，罔計賢否，悉拔而登之，一視同仁。

translations.literal: If one says Your Majesty favors and benefits the solitary, poor, and long-stagnant scholars, without considering worthy or unworthy, pulling them all up and elevating them, treating all alike with one kindness—
translations.idiomatic: Some say Your Majesty favors the poor and long-neglected scholars, without regard to merit, elevating them all alike—

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂此非確論。

translations.literal: your subject privately considers that this is not a sound argument.
translations.idiomatic: your subject respectfully submits that this is not sound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖人在上，則內君子而外小人。

translations.literal: For when a sage is above, then within are gentlemen and without are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When a sage rules above, he keeps gentlemen close and petty men at a distance.

sentences.zh: 若薰蕕同器，甚非所以正人倫、淳風俗也。

translations.literal: If fragrant and foul share one vessel, this is very far from the means to rectify human relations and purify custom.
translations.idiomatic: To mix the fragrant with the foul in one vessel is far from the way to rectify human relations and purify custom.

sentences.zh: 況丘園之下，豈無宏才茂德之士。

translations.literal: Moreover, beneath hills and gardens, are there not men of great talent and flourishing virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among those living in seclusion, are there not men of great talent and flourishing virtue?

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能設科以擢異等之士，俾陳古今之治亂、君臣之得失、生民之休戚、賢愚之用舍，庶幾有益於治，不特詩賦、論策之小技，以應有司之求而已。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly establish an examination to raise men of extraordinary grade, causing them to set forth the order and disorder of past and present, the gains and losses of ruler and minister, the weal and woe of the people, and the employment and dismissal of worthy and foolish, then perhaps there will be benefit to governance—not merely the minor skills of poetry, rhapsodies, essays, and policy plans to meet the requests of the officials."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would truly establish an examination to raise men of extraordinary talent, having them address the order and disorder of past and present, the successes and failures of rulers and ministers, the welfare and suffering of the people, and the employment and dismissal of the worthy and the foolish, then governance might truly benefit—not merely the minor skills of poetry and policy essays to satisfy the examining officials."

sentences.zh: 疏上，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the memorial, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，復舉進士，廷試，方禹中獻賦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he again took the jinshi examination; at the palace examination Fang Yu was presenting a rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he again sat for the jinshi examination; at the palace examination Fang Yu was presenting his rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 太宗召升殿，詢其門第，賜甲科，解褐大名府觀察推官。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned him up to the hall, inquired about his family standing, granted the top grade, and upon leaving office dress he became investigating clerk of the Daming prefectural observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned him to the hall, inquired about his family background, granted him the top grade, and on entering service appointed him investigating clerk of the Daming observation commission.

sentences.zh: 四年，與梁湛並召為右拾遺、直史館，賜緋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he and Liang Zhan were together summoned as Right Reminder and attached to the Historiography Institute, and granted crimson.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he and Liang Zhan were summoned together as Right Reminder with a concurrent post at the Historiography Institute, and granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 判鼓司、登聞院。

translations.literal: He judged the Drum Office and the Court of Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of the Drum Office and the Court of Imperial Audience.

sentences.zh: 顥在大名佐趙昌言。

translations.literal: Hao at Daming assisted Zhao Changyan.
translations.idiomatic: At Daming, Hao served as assistant to Zhao Changyan.

sentences.zh: 昌言入掌樞密，會翟馬周事，顥坐貶虢州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Changyan entered to direct the Bureau of Military Affairs; when the Zhai Ma Zhou affair occurred, Hao was implicated and demoted to revenue adjutant of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Changyan entered the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Zhai Ma Zhou affair broke out and Hao was implicated and demoted to revenue adjutant of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 起知魚臺縣，就加大理評事。

translations.literal: He was raised to be magistrate of Yutai County and on the spot additionally made an evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed magistrate of Yutai County and at the same time promoted to evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 召還，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: He was recalled and moved to director within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was promoted to director within the palace.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復直史館，歷開封府推官、三司關西道判官，轉太常博士，丁內艱，起令赴職，改右司諫。

translations.literal: Before long he again was attached to the Historiography Institute, passed through investigating clerk of the Kaifeng prefecture and transport-assessor of the Guanxi circuit of the Three Departments, was changed to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, mourned his mother, was raised and ordered to take office, and was changed to remonstrance officer of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again attached to the Historiography Institute, served as investigating clerk of Kaifeng and transport-assessor on the Guanxi circuit of the Three Departments, and was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. After mourning his mother he was recalled to duty and appointed remonstrance officer of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，詔群臣言事，顥時使陝西，途中作《聽政箴》以獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign an edict ordered the ministers to speak on affairs; Hao was then on mission to Shaanxi and on the road composed the Admonition on Hearing Government to present.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign the court ordered ministers to speak freely on state affairs; Hao was then on mission to Shaanxi and composed the Admonition on Hearing Government on the road to present to the throne.

sentences.zh: 還為度支判官。

translations.literal: On his return he became revenue-assessor.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed revenue-assessor.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，與楊勵、李若拙、朱台符同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping he served with Yang Li, Li Ruozhuo, and Zhu Taifu as co-supervisor of the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianping he served with Yang Li, Li Ruozhuo, and Zhu Taifu as co-supervisor of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 時詔錢若水重修《太祖實錄》，表顥參其事，又同修起居注。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered Qian Ruoshui to revise the Veritable Records of Taizu; Hao was memorialized to participate in the task, and also jointly compiled the Records of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Qian Ruoshui to revise the Veritable Records of Taizu; Hao was nominated to assist and also helped compile the Records of the Emperor's Movements.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕大名，詔訪群臣邊事，顥上疏曰：

translations.literal: Escorting the imperial carriage at Daming, an edict sought the ministers' views on frontier affairs; Hao submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: While escorting the imperial carriage at Daming, the emperor sought the ministers' views on frontier affairs; Hao submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞自古用兵之道，在乎明賞罰而已。

translations.literal: "Your subject has heard that the way of employing troops since antiquity lies only in making rewards and punishments clear.
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject has heard that since antiquity the art of war has rested on making rewards and punishments clear.

sentences.zh: 然而賞不可以獨任，罰不可以少失。

translations.literal: Yet rewards cannot be borne alone, and punishments cannot suffer the slightest lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rewards cannot be dispensed alone, and punishments cannot suffer the slightest lapse.

sentences.zh: 故《兵法》曰：『罰之不行，譬如驕子之不可用。

translations.literal: Therefore the Art of War says: 'When punishments are not carried out, it is like a spoiled child who cannot be used.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Art of War says: 'When punishments are not enforced, it is like a spoiled child who cannot be used.'

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『善為將者，威振敵國，令行三軍。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'A general who excels makes his authority shake enemy states and his orders run through the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: ' It also says: 'A capable general makes his authority shake enemy states and his orders prevail throughout the three armies.

sentences.zh: 盡忠益時者，雖仇必賞；

translations.literal: Those who exhaust loyalty and benefit the age, though enemies, must be rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: Those who serve with full loyalty, though they be enemies, must be rewarded;

sentences.zh: 犯法敗事者，雖親必罰。

translations.literal: those who violate law and ruin affairs, though kin, must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: and those who break the law and ruin affairs, though they be kin, must be punished.

sentences.zh: 』故孫武斬隊長而兵皆整，穰苴斬監軍而敵遂退。

translations.literal: ' Therefore Sun Wu beheaded the company commander and the troops were all ordered; Rang Ju beheaded the army supervisor and the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thus Sun Wu beheaded a company commander and his troops fell into perfect order; Rang Ju beheaded an army supervisor and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，兵法不可不正也。

translations.literal: Spoken in this way, military law cannot but be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that military law must be enforced with strict justice.

sentences.zh: 昨者命將出師，乘秋備塞，而傅潛奉明詔，握重兵，逗撓無謀，守陴玩寇，老精兵於不用。

translations.literal: Recently generals were ordered to take the field, taking advantage of autumn to prepare the frontier defenses, yet Fu Qian received the clear edict, held heavy troops, dallied and hesitated without plan, guarded the ramparts and toyed with the enemy, and aged elite troops in disuse.
translations.idiomatic: Recently generals were sent to take the field in autumn to secure the frontier, yet Fu Qian, though he held the emperor's clear command and heavy forces, dallied without plan, held the walls and toyed with the enemy, and let his best troops grow stale from disuse.

sentences.zh: 以至蕃馬南牧，邊塵晝驚，河朔之民，流移失所，魏博以北，蹂踐一空。

translations.literal: The result was that barbarian horses pastured southward, frontier dust alarmed by day, the people of Heshuo were displaced and lost their homes, and north of Weibo was trampled utterly empty.
translations.idiomatic: The result was that barbarian horses ranged southward, frontier alarms rose by day, the people of Heshuo were driven from their homes, and the country north of Weibo was trampled utterly bare.

sentences.zh: 遂至殘妖未殄，鑾輅親征，此所謂以賊遺君父者也。

translations.literal: It reached the point that lingering rebels were not destroyed and the imperial carriage went on campaign in person—this is what is called leaving the bandits as a legacy to the ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: It reached the point that the rebels were not destroyed and the emperor himself took the field—this is what is meant by leaving the enemy as a burden upon one's sovereign and father.

sentences.zh: 乃或赦而不問，則何以謝橫死之民；

translations.literal: If now he is pardoned and not investigated, how can one answer to the people who died violently;
translations.idiomatic: If he is now pardoned and not held to account, how can the court answer to the people who died by violence;

sentences.zh: 或黜而不戮，則何以恢用兵之略。

translations.literal: or if he is dismissed but not executed, how can one restore the strategy of employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: or if he is dismissed but not executed, how can the strategy of war be restored?

sentences.zh: 以軍法論之，固合斬潛以徇軍中，降詔以示天下。

translations.literal: Judged by military law, he should indeed be beheaded to display discipline in the army and an edict lowered to show All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: By military law he should be beheaded to display discipline in the army, and an edict issued to show the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 如此，則協前古之典章，戒後來之將帥，然後擇邊臣之可用者，就委用之。

translations.literal: In this way one would accord with the statutes of former antiquity, warn later generals and commanders, and then select frontier officials who can be used and commission them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the court would accord with the statutes of antiquity, warn future commanders, and then select capable frontier officials and commission them.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗讀漢史，李廣之屯兵行師也，無部伍行陣，就善水草，人人自便，不擊刁斗以自衛，遠於斥候，未嘗遇害，而廣終為名將，士卒樂用。

translations.literal: Your subject once read the Han histories: when Li Guang encamped and marched his army, there were no companies, ranks, or battle lines; he sought good grass and water, each man made himself comfortable, did not strike the watch-clapper for self-defense, kept scouts far away, and never suffered harm; yet Guang in the end became a famed general and the soldiers were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has read in the Han histories that when Li Guang encamped and marched, he kept no formal companies or battle lines, sought good pasture and water, let each man find his own comfort, did not sound the watch-clappers for self-defense, and kept scouts far afield—yet he never suffered harm, became a famed general, and his men were glad to follow him.

sentences.zh: 又唐高祖之備北邊也，選頸兵為遊騎，不齎軍糧，隨逐水草，遇敵則殺，當時以為得策。

translations.literal: Again, when Tang Gaozu prepared the northern frontier, he selected neck troops as roaming cavalry, carried no army grain, followed grass and water, and killed when they met the enemy; at the time this was considered a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Gaozu prepared the northern frontier, he selected elite troops as roaming cavalry who carried no army grain, followed grass and water, and struck the enemy when they met—at the time this was considered an excellent strategy.

sentences.zh: 願於邊將中，不以名位高卑，但擇其武勇謀略素為眾所推服者，取十人焉。

translations.literal: I wish that among frontier generals, without regard to the height or lowness of name and rank, one select only those whose martial valor and stratagems have long been admired by the multitude, and take ten men.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that among frontier generals, without regard to rank, ten men be chosen whose martial valor and strategic ability have long won the respect of the troops.

sentences.zh: 人付騎士五十，器甲完備，輕齎糧糗，逐水草以為利，往復扞禦。

translations.literal: To each man give fifty horsemen, complete weapons and armor, light carriage of dry provisions, following grass and water for advantage, going back and forth to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Give each man fifty horsemen with complete arms and armor, light provisions, and orders to follow grass and water and ride back and forth to defend the frontier.

sentences.zh: 不令入郡邑，不許聚處，遇有寇兵，隨時掩捕。

translations.literal: Do not allow them to enter prefectures and districts, do not permit them to gather and stay together; when bandit troops appear, strike and capture at once.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let them enter towns or gather in one place; when raiders appear, strike and capture them at once.

sentences.zh: 仍令烽候相望，交相救應。

translations.literal: Further order beacon posts to face one another and mutually rescue and respond.
translations.idiomatic: Further, let beacon posts face one another so that they can rescue and support each other.

sentences.zh: 緣邊州郡守城兵帥，即堅壁以待之。

translations.literal: The prefectures and districts along the frontier that guard cities and command garrison troops should at once hold the walls firm and wait.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier prefectures and their garrison commanders should hold their walls firm and wait.

sentences.zh: 遇遊騎近城，掩殺邊寇，內量出兵甲援救。

translations.literal: When roaming cavalry approach a city, strike and kill frontier raiders, and from within measure out troops and armor to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When roaming cavalry approach a city, they should strike the raiders, and the garrison should send out troops as needed to support them.

sentences.zh: 如此，則乘城者不堅閉壘門，免坐觀於勝負；

translations.literal: In this way those who mount the walls need not firmly shut the camp gates and be spared sitting and watching the outcome;
translations.idiomatic: In this way the defenders need not shut their gates tight and sit idle watching the outcome of battle;

sentences.zh: 捍邊者不苟依郡郭，可行備於寇攘。

translations.literal: those who defend the frontier need not cling carelessly to prefectural walls and can carry out preparations against raiding enemies.
translations.idiomatic: and the frontier defenders need not cling passively to the walls but can take active measures against raiders.

sentences.zh: 雖匪良籌，且殊膠柱。」

translations.literal: Though this is not a fine plan, it is still quite unlike fixing the peg on a zither."
translations.idiomatic: Though this may not be the finest plan, it is still far better than rigid inflexibility."

sentences.zh: 時論頗稱之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion greatly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion greatly praised the memorial.

sentences.zh: 三年，與李宗諤、趙安仁並命知制誥，賜金紫，是年冬，王均平，命為峽路安撫使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was with Li Zong'e and Zhao Anren together ordered to draft imperial edicts and granted gold and purple; that winter Wang Jun was pacified, and he was ordered to be pacification commissioner of the Xia circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he and Li Zong'e and Zhao Anren were appointed together to draft imperial edicts and granted gold and purple insignia. That winter, after Wang Jun's rebellion was pacified, Hao was appointed pacification commissioner of the Xia circuit.

sentences.zh: 歸掌三班。

translations.literal: On his return he directed the Three Classes.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he took charge of the Three Classes.

sentences.zh: 韓國華判大理，以斷刑失中，乃選顥以代之。

translations.literal: Han Guohua judged the Court of Judicial Review and because his criminal judgments missed the mean, Hao was selected to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guohua presided over the Court of Judicial Review but his criminal judgments were faulty, so Hao was chosen to replace him.

sentences.zh: 四年，張齊賢使關右安撫，以顥為之副。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhang Qixian was envoy for Guanxi pacification, with Hao as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhang Qixian was sent to pacify Guanxi, with Hao as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 顥有吏才，每進對，詞辯明敏，真宗嘉賞之。

translations.literal: Hao had talent for administration; whenever he advanced for audience his words and debate were clear and keen, and Zhenzong praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had a gift for administration; whenever he appeared before the throne his replies were clear and keen, and Zhenzong greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 凡群臣上封者，悉付顥洎薛映詳閱可否。

translations.literal: All sealed memorials from the ministers were entirely handed to Hao and Xue Ying to examine in detail for approval or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: All sealed memorials from the ministers were handed to Hao and Xue Ying to review for approval or rejection.

sentences.zh: 冬，以河北饑盜，命與映分為東、西路巡檢使。

translations.literal: In winter, because of famine and banditry in Hebei, he was ordered with Ying to divide into eastern and western route inspection commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, because of famine and banditry in Hebei, he and Ying were appointed inspection commissioners for the eastern and western routes respectively.

sentences.zh: 還，拜右諫議大夫，充戶部使。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and made commissioner of the Households Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and commissioner of the Households Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會罷三部使，以顥為翰林學士同知審官院、三班。

translations.literal: When the three department commissioners were abolished, Hao was made Hanlin academician and co-director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Three Classes.
translations.idiomatic: When the three department commissioners were abolished, Hao was appointed Hanlin academician with concurrent charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Three Classes.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，權知開封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde he acted as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde he served as acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 顥美風姿，強力少疾，閨門雍睦。

translations.literal: Hao had fine bearing, was strong and vigorous and seldom ill, and his inner quarters were harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had a fine presence, was strong and vigorous and seldom fell ill, and his household was harmonious.

sentences.zh: 與人交久而無改，士大夫多之。

translations.literal: In dealings with others he was long unchanged, and many scholar-officials esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he was steadfast over long years, and many scholar-officials esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 六月，暴病卒，年九十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he died suddenly of illness, aged ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he died suddenly of illness, at the age of ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 上甚軫惻，賜贈加等。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply grieved and compassionate and granted posthumous gifts of added rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and granted posthumous honors of added rank.

sentences.zh: 所著文集十五卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings amounted to fifteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to fifteen juan.

sentences.zh: 子：固、述、適。

translations.literal: His sons: Gu, Shu, and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Gu, Shu, and Shi.

sentences.zh: 適相仁宗，別有傳。

translations.literal: Shi became chief minister to Renzong and has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shi became chief minister to Emperor Renzong and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 子 固

translations.literal: Son: Gu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Gu

sentences.zh: 固，字仲堅。

translations.literal: Gu, style name Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, courtesy name Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 幼有志節，嘗著《漢春秋》，顥器賞之。

translations.literal: From youth he had resolve and integrity; he once composed the Spring and Autumn of Han, and Hao valued and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed resolve and integrity; he wrote the Spring and Autumn of Han, which his father greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 初，以顥遺蔭，賜進士出身。

translations.literal: At first, through Hao's posthumous favor, he was granted jinshi origin.
translations.idiomatic: At first, through his father's posthumous privilege, he was granted jinshi status.

sentences.zh: 服闋，詣登聞院讓前命，願赴鄉舉，許之。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he went to the Court of Imperial Audience to decline the prior appointment, wishing to take the provincial examination, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he went to the Court of Imperial Audience to decline the prior appointment and asked to sit for the provincial examination; the court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，舉服勤詞學科，擢甲第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he took the examination in diligent service and literary studies and was raised to the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he took the special examination in diligent service and literary studies and placed at the top of the list.

sentences.zh: 解褐將作監丞、同判密州，就遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office dress he was made vice director of the Directorate of Works and concurrent judge of Mi Prefecture, and on the spot was moved to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he was appointed vice director of the Directorate of Works and concurrent judge of Mi Prefecture, and at the same time promoted to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，改著作郎、直史館，賜緋。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was changed to compiler and attached to the Historiography Institute, and granted crimson.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed compiler with a concurrent post at the Historiography Institute and granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部判官、判戶部勾院。

translations.literal: He passed through revenue-assessor of the Households Ministry and judge of the Households Ministry audit office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as revenue-assessor of the Households Ministry and judge of the Households Ministry audit office.

sentences.zh: 為人氣調俊爽，善與人交，疏財慷慨，尚氣義，明於吏道。

translations.literal: As a man his spirit and tone were handsome and bright; he was good at friendship, liberal with wealth and generous, valued integrity and righteousness, and was clear in the ways of administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was spirited and open in manner, skilled in friendship, generous with wealth, devoted to integrity, and clear-sighted in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 馬元方領三司，臨事粗率，固摭其曠闕之狀，屢請對條奏。

translations.literal: Ma Yuanfang directed the Three Departments and was coarse and careless in handling affairs; Gu gathered accounts of his neglects and omissions and repeatedly requested audience to present them item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuanfang directed the Three Departments but was coarse and careless in affairs; Gu collected accounts of his neglects and repeatedly requested audience to present them in detail.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔鞠獄，時稱平審。

translations.literal: He was once ordered by edict to try cases, and the age called his judgments fair and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered by edict to try cases, and his contemporaries praised his judgments as fair and thorough.

sentences.zh: 天禧大禮成，奏頌甚工。

translations.literal: When the great rites of Tianxi were completed, his submitted eulogy was very skillful.
translations.idiomatic: When the great rites of Tianxi were completed, the eulogy he submitted was highly accomplished.

sentences.zh: 無幾卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 楊徽之

translations.literal: Yang Huizhi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huizhi

sentences.zh: 楊徽之，字仲猷，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Yang Huizhi, style name Zhongyou, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huizhi, courtesy name Zhongyou, was from Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖郜，仕閩為義軍校。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gao served Min as an officer of the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gao served Min as an officer of the righteous army.

sentences.zh: 家世尚武，父澄獨折節為儒，終浦城令。

translations.literal: The family for generations honored martial affairs; his father Cheng alone bent his will to become a Confucian and ended as magistrate of Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The family had for generations honored martial pursuits; his father Cheng alone turned to Confucian learning and ended his career as magistrate of Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 徽之幼刻苦為學，邑人江文蔚善賦，江為能詩，徽之與之遊從，遂與齊名。

translations.literal: Huizhi from youth studied bitterly and hard; a townsman Jiang Wenwei excelled at rhapsodies, and Jiang Wei was skilled at poetry; Huizhi associated with them in travel and companionship and thus became equally famed.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Huizhi studied with bitter diligence. His townsman Jiang Wenwei excelled at rhapsodies and Jiang Wei at poetry; Huizhi associated with them and soon shared equal fame.

sentences.zh: 嘗肄業於潯陽廬山，時李氏據有江表，乃潛服至汴、洛，以文投竇儀、王朴，深賞遇之。

translations.literal: He once pursued studies at Lushan in Xunyang; at the time the Li house held the lands south of the Yangtze, so he secretly traveled in plain dress to Bian and Luoyang, presented his writings to Dou Yi and Wang Pu, and was deeply appreciated and favored.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied at Lushan in Xunyang. When the Li regime held the lands south of the Yangtze, he secretly traveled to Bian and Luoyang, presented his writings to Dou Yi and Wang Pu, and won their deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，舉進士，劉溫叟知貢部，中甲科。

translations.literal: During Xiande of Zhou he took the jinshi examination; Liu Wensou directed the examination bureau, and he placed in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era of Zhou he took the jinshi examination; Liu Wensou presided over the examinations, and Huizhi placed in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 同時登第者十六人，世宗命覆試，惟徽之與李覃、何嚴、趙鄰幾中選。

translations.literal: Sixteen passed the examination at the same time; Shizong ordered a re-examination, and only Huizhi with Li Tan, He Yan, and Zhao Linji were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen men passed at the same time; Emperor Shizong ordered a re-examination, and only Huizhi, Li Tan, He Yan, and Zhao Linji were selected.

sentences.zh: 解褐校書郎、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office dress he was made proofreader and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he was appointed proofreader and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 宰相范質深器重之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Fan Zhi deeply valued and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Fan Zhi greatly valued and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 歷著作佐郎、右拾遺。

translations.literal: He passed through assistant compiler and Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant compiler and Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 竇儼纂禮樂書，徽之預焉。

translations.literal: Dou Yan compiled the book on rites and music, and Huizhi participated in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Yan compiled the book on rites and music, Huizhi took part in the work.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，與鄭玘並出為天興令，府帥王彥超素知其名，待以賓禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he and Zheng Qi were together sent out as magistrates of Tianxing; the prefectural commander Wang Yanchao had long known his name and treated him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qiande he and Zheng Qi were sent out together as magistrates of Tianxing; the prefectural commander Wang Yanchao had long known his reputation and treated him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，移峨眉令。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was moved to be magistrate of Emei.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was transferred to magistrate of Emei.

sentences.zh: 時宋白宰玉津，多以吟詠酬答。

translations.literal: At the time Song Bai governed Yujin, and they often answered one another in chanting and singing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Song Bai governed Yujin, and the two often exchanged poems.

sentences.zh: 復為著作佐郎、知全州，就遷左拾遺、右補闕。

translations.literal: He again became assistant compiler and prefect of Quan, and on the spot was moved to Left Reminder and Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He again became assistant compiler and prefect of Quan, and at the same time was promoted to Left Reminder and Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，代還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he returned upon completing his acting term.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taiping Xingguo era, he returned after completing his tour of duty.

sentences.zh: 太宗素聞其詩名，因索所著。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong had long heard his fame in poetry and therefore sought his compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had long known of his reputation as a poet and asked to see his writings.

sentences.zh: 徽之以數百篇奏御，且獻詩為謝，其卒章有「十年流落今何幸，叨遇君王問姓名」 語。

translations.literal: Huizhi submitted several hundred pieces to the throne, and moreover presented a poem in thanks; its final stanza had the words, "Ten years adrift and fallen—what fortune today, that I undeservedly meet the sovereign asking my name."
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi submitted several hundred poems to the throne and also offered a poem of thanks whose closing lines read, "Ten years in wandering exile—what luck today that the king asks my name."

sentences.zh: 太宗覽之稱賞，自是聖製多以別本為賜。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong read them and commended them; from then on imperial compositions were mostly given him in separate copies as presents.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong read them with praise, and thereafter often granted him duplicate copies of his own imperial compositions.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史、權判刑部。

translations.literal: He was moved to attending censor and acting judge of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending censor and acting judge of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 嘗屬疾，遣尚醫診療，賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Once when afflicted with illness, the court sent an imperial physician to diagnose and treat him, and granted three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: When he once fell ill, the court sent an imperial physician to treat him and granted him three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 轉庫部員外郎，賜金紫，判南曹，同知京朝官差遣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to outer bureau director of the Treasury Ministry, granted gold-purple insignia, assigned to judge the Southern Bureau, and made co-administrator of assignments for metropolitan officials.
translations.idiomatic: He became outer bureau director of the Treasury Ministry, was granted gold-and-purple insignia, served as judge of the Southern Bureau, and was appointed co-director of assignments for capital officials.

sentences.zh: 會詔李昉等采緝前代文字，類為《文苑英華》，以徽之精於風雅，分命編詩，為百八十卷。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered Li Fang and others to gather and compile writings of former ages, classified into the Wen yuan ying hua, because Huizhi was skilled in refined letters, he was separately ordered to compile poetry, making one hundred eighty juan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fang and others were ordered to collect texts of earlier dynasties for the Wen yuan ying hua, Huizhi's mastery of literary refinement earned him charge of the poetry section, which ran to one hundred and eighty juan.

sentences.zh: 歷遷刑、兵二部郎中。

translations.literal: He successively moved through bureau director posts in the Ministries of Justice and War.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as bureau director in both the Ministries of Justice and War.

sentences.zh: 獻《雍熙詞》，上賡其韻以賜。

translations.literal: He presented the Yongxi Ci; the sovereign continued its rhyme and granted it as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the Yongxi Ci, and the emperor continued the rhyme in reply and granted it to him as a gift.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，拜左諫議大夫，出知許州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he received appointment as Left Remonstrance Grandee and went out as prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was appointed Left Remonstrance Grandee and sent out to serve as prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入判史館事，加修撰。

translations.literal: He entered to judge History Office affairs and was given the additional post of compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital to direct the History Office and was additionally appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 因次對上言，曰：「自陛下嗣統鴻圖，闡揚文治，廢墜修舉，儒學響臻，乃至周岩野以聘隱淪，盛科選以來才彥，取士之道，亦已至矣。

translations.literal: Seizing a subsequent audience he addressed the Sovereign, saying: "Since Your Majesty succeeded to the imperial design, unfolded civil governance, restored neglected institutions, and Confucian learning resounded in response—even to searching cliffs and wilds to invite the hidden and fallen, and magnifying examination selection to summon talented men—the way of obtaining scholars has already reached fullness."
translations.idiomatic: Taking advantage of a subsequent audience he addressed the emperor, saying: "Since Your Majesty succeeded to the great design, extended civil governance, restored what had fallen into neglect, and brought Confucian learning ringing in response—even to the point of searching cliff and field to invite the hidden and obscure, and magnifying the examination system to draw in men of talent—the way of selecting scholars has already reached its fullness."

sentences.zh: 然擅文章者多超遷，明經業者罕殊用，向非振舉，曷勸專勤，師法不傳，祖述安在！

translations.literal: Yet those skilled in literary composition are often promoted beyond measure, while those who clarify the classics are rarely given distinctive employment; if we do not raise them up and recommend them, how shall we encourage single-minded diligence? If the master's teaching is not transmitted, where shall the inheritance of the ancients be!
translations.idiomatic: Yet those skilled in literary composition are often promoted beyond measure, while those devoted to the classics are rarely given distinctive employment. If we do not raise them up and recommend them, how shall we encourage single-minded diligence? If the master's teaching is not transmitted, where shall the inheritance of the ancients be!

sentences.zh: 且京師四方之會，太學首善之地。

translations.literal: Moreover the capital is the gathering place of all four directions, and the Imperial Academy is the foremost seat of excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the capital is where all four directions converge, and the Imperial Academy is the foremost seat of learning.

sentences.zh: 今五經博士，並闕其員，非所以崇教化、獎人材、繇內及外之道也。

translations.literal: Now the Five Classics doctorate posts all lack incumbents—this is not the way to exalt instruction and transformation, reward talent, or extend influence from within to without.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Five Classics doctorate posts all stand vacant—this is not the way to exalt instruction, reward talent, or extend influence from within to without.

sentences.zh: 伏望浚發明詔，博求通經之士，簡之朝著，拔自草萊，增置員數，分教胄子，隨其所業，授以本官，廩稍且優，旌別斯在。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will issue a clarifying edict, broadly seek men thoroughly versed in the classics, select them at court, pluck them from among common fields, increase the number of posts, assign them to teach the imperial clansmen according to their specialties, grant them their proper official titles, provide generous stipends, and thereby distinguish and honor them.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will issue a clarifying edict, broadly seek men thoroughly versed in the classics, select them at court, pluck them from humble origins, increase the number of posts, assign them to teach the imperial clansmen according to their specialties, grant them their proper official titles, provide generous stipends, and thereby distinguish and honor them.

sentences.zh: 淹貫之士，既蒙厚賞，則天下善類知所勸矣，無使唐、漢專稱得人。

translations.literal: When thoroughly accomplished scholars receive generous rewards, then all worthy men under heaven will know what to strive for—do not let Tang and Han alone be praised for obtaining talent.
translations.idiomatic: When thoroughly accomplished scholars receive generous rewards, all worthy men under heaven will know what to strive for—do not let Tang and Han alone be praised for obtaining talent.

sentences.zh: 」太宗嘉納之，顧謂宰相曰：「徽之儒雅，操履無玷，置於館閣宜矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong praised and accepted this, and turning to the chief ministers said: "Huizhi is refined and cultivated, his conduct without blemish—it is fitting to place him in the Hall of Assembled Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong praised and accepted the memorial, and turning to the chief ministers said, "Huizhi is refined and cultivated, his conduct without blemish—it is fitting to place him in the Hall of Assembled Worthies."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，改判集賢院。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to direct the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to direct the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔預觀燈乾元樓，上嘉其精力不衰。

translations.literal: Once by edict he was invited to watch the lanterns at Qianyuan Tower; the sovereign commended that his vigor had not waned.
translations.idiomatic: Once by edict he was invited to watch the lanterns at Qianyuan Tower; the emperor commended that his vigor had not waned.

sentences.zh: 時劉昌言拔自下位，不逾時參掌機務，懼無以厭人望，常求自安之計。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Changyan had been pulled up from low rank and within no time shared in core affairs of state; fearing he could not satisfy public expectation, he constantly sought some plan to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Changyan had been pulled up from low rank and within no time shared in core affairs of state; fearing he could not satisfy public expectation, he constantly sought some plan to secure himself.

sentences.zh: 董儼為右計使，欲傾昌言代之，嘗謂徽之曰：「上遇張洎、錢若水甚厚，旦夕將大用。

translations.literal: Dong Yan served as Right Fiscal Commissioner and wished to overturn Changyan and replace him; he once said to Huizhi: "The sovereign treats Zhang Zhi and Qian Ruoshui with great favor—they will soon be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yan served as Right Fiscal Commissioner and wished to overturn Changyan and replace him; he once said to Huizhi, "The emperor treats Zhang Zhi and Qian Ruoshui with great favor—they will soon be greatly employed."

sentences.zh: 」有直史館錢熙者，與昌言厚善，詣徽之，徽之語次及之。

translations.literal: Qian Xi, who held direct appointment in the History Office, was on close terms with Changyan; he visited Huizhi, and in the course of conversation Huizhi mentioned this.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xi, who held direct appointment in the History Office, was on close terms with Changyan; he visited Huizhi, and in the course of conversation Huizhi mentioned this.

sentences.zh: 熙遽以告昌言，昌言以告洎。

translations.literal: Xi immediately told Changyan, and Changyan told Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi immediately told Changyan, and Changyan told Zhi.

sentences.zh: 洎方固寵，謂徽之遣熙構飛語中傷己，遂白上。

translations.literal: Zhi was then securing imperial favor and believed Huizhi had sent Xi to fabricate slanderous rumors to injure him, and so reported this to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was then securing imperial favor and believed Huizhi had sent Xi to fabricate slanderous rumors to injure him, and so reported this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上怒，召昌言質其語。

translations.literal: The sovereign grew angry and summoned Changyan to verify the words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and summoned Changyan to verify the words.

sentences.zh: 出徽之為山南東道行軍司馬，熙落職通判朗州。

translations.literal: Huizhi was sent out as military aide of the Shan'nandong Circuit; Xi was stripped of office and made supervisory commissioner of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi was sent out as military aide of the Shan'nandong Circuit; Xi was stripped of office and made supervisory commissioner of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽之未行，改鎮安軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Before Huizhi departed he was reassigned as military aide of Zhen'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before Huizhi departed he was reassigned as military aide of Zhen'an Army.

sentences.zh: 真宗尹京，妙選僚佐，驛召為左諫議大夫，與畢士安並充開封府判官，召對便殿，諭以輔導意。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong held charge of the capital, he carefully selected aides; Huizhi was summoned by post horse as Left Remonstrance Grandee and, together with Bi Shi'an, appointed judge of Kaifeng Prefecture; summoned to audience in the Informal Hall, he was instructed in the intent of guidance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong held charge of the capital, he carefully selected aides; Huizhi was summoned by post horse as Left Remonstrance Grandee and, together with Bi Shi'an, appointed judge of Kaifeng Prefecture; summoned to audience in the Informal Hall, he was instructed in the intent of guidance and instruction.

sentences.zh: 東宮建屬，以徽之兼左庶子。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established with its staff, Huizhi was made concurrent Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was established with its staff, Huizhi was made concurrent Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嘗出巡田，真宗作詩言懷，因以寄之。

translations.literal: Once when he went out on an inspection tour of the fields, Zhenzong composed a poem voicing his feelings and sent it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he went out on an inspection tour of the fields, Zhenzong composed a poem voicing his feelings and sent it to him.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 即位，拜工部侍郎、樞密直學士，俄兼秘書監。

translations.literal: Upon accession he was appointed Vice Minister of Works, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon also Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Upon accession he was appointed Vice Minister of Works, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon also Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，加禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二年春，以衰疾求解近職，改兵部，仍兼秘書監，入謝，命坐，勞之曰：「圖書之府，清淨無事，俾卿得以養性也。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, citing age and illness he requested relief from a proximate office; he was transferred to the Ministry of War while still holding the Secretariat directorship; entering to give thanks, he was ordered to sit; the sovereign comforted him, saying: "The house of books is quiet and without business—there you may nourish your nature."
