translations.idiomatic: In the second year, spring, citing age and illness he requested relief from a proximate office; he was transferred to the Ministry of War while still holding the Secretariat directorship; entering to give thanks, he was ordered to sit; the emperor comforted him, saying, "The house of books is quiet and without business—there you may nourish your nature."

sentences.zh: 」是秋，特置翰林侍讀學士，命與夏侯嶠、呂文仲並為之，賜宴秘閣，且褒以詩。

translations.literal: That autumn a Hanlin Attendant Reader academician post was specially established; he was ordered to serve together with Xiahou Qiao and Lü Wenshong; a banquet was granted at the Secret Library and he was also praised with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a Hanlin Attendant Reader academician post was specially established; he was ordered to serve together with Xiahou Qiao and Lü Wenshong; a banquet was granted at the Secret Library and he was also praised with a poem.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以足疾請告，上取名藥以賜。

translations.literal: Before long, citing foot ailment he requested leave; the sovereign selected famous medicines and granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, citing foot ailment he requested leave; the emperor selected famous medicines and granted them.

sentences.zh: 郊祀不及扈從，錫齎如侍祠之例。

translations.literal: Unable to accompany the suburban sacrifice, he received gifts according to the precedent for those attending the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to accompany the suburban sacrifice, he received gifts according to the precedent for those attending the rites.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，徽之力疾辭於苑中。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured north, Huizhi, though ill, declined in the palace garden.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage toured north, Huizhi, though ill, declined in the palace garden.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂曰：「卿勉進醫藥，比見，當不久也。

translations.literal: The sovereign turning to him said: "Sir, take your medicines diligently; when we next meet, it should not be long."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turning to him said, "Sir, take your medicines diligently; when we next meet, it should not be long."

sentences.zh: 」及駐蹕大名，特降手詔存諭。

translations.literal: When the halt was made at Daming, a special handwritten edict was sent down to comfort and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: When the halt was made at Daming, a special handwritten edict was sent down to comfort and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 明年春正月，車駕還，又遣使臨問。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following spring, when the imperial carriage returned, another envoy was sent to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following spring, when the imperial carriage returned, another envoy was sent to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書，賜其家錢五十萬，絹五百匹。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Minister of War; his family was granted five hundred thousand in cash and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of War; his family was granted five hundred thousand cash and five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 錄其外孫宋綬太常寺太祝，侄孫偃、集並同學究出身。

translations.literal: His grandson by a daughter Song Shou was recorded as Director of Solemnity in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his grand-nephews Yan and Ji were both given the jinshi-by-study status.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson by a daughter Song Shou was recorded as Director of Solemnity in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his grand-nephews Yan and Ji were both given the jinshi-by-study status.

sentences.zh: 徽之純厚清介，守規矩，尚名教，尤疾非道以幹進者。

translations.literal: Huizhi was pure, thick-hearted, and clean-integrity; he kept to rules and measured conduct, honored orthodox teaching, and especially despised those who used improper ways to press for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi was pure-hearted and incorruptible; he kept to rules and measured conduct, honored orthodox teaching, and especially despised those who used improper means to press for advancement.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「溫仲舒、寇準用搏擊取貴位，使後輩務習趨競，禮俗浸薄。

translations.literal: He once said: "Wen Zhongshu and Kou Zhun used aggressive attack to win exalted rank, causing later generations to devote themselves to scrambling competition, and ritual custom gradually grew thin."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Wen Zhongshu and Kou Zhun used aggressive attack to win exalted rank, causing later generations to devote themselves to scrambling competition, and ritual custom gradually grew thin."

sentences.zh: 」世謂其知言。

translations.literal: The age called this knowing speech.
translations.idiomatic: The age called this knowing speech.

sentences.zh: 徽之寡諧於俗，唯李昉、王祐深所推服，與石熙載、李穆、賈黃中為文義友。

translations.literal: Huizhi had little harmony with vulgar ways; only Li Fang and Wang You deeply admired and submitted to him; with Shi Xizai, Li Mu, and Jia Huangzhong he was friends united in literary principle.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi had little harmony with vulgar ways; only Li Fang and Wang You deeply admired and submitted to him; with Shi Xizai, Li Mu, and Jia Huangzhong he was friends united in literary principle.

sentences.zh: 自為郎官、御史，朝廷即待以舊德。

translations.literal: From the time he became a bureau director or censor, the court already treated him with respect for established virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he became a bureau director or censor, the court already treated him with respect for established virtue.

sentences.zh: 善談論，多識典故，唐室以來士族人物，悉能詳記。

translations.literal: He was skilled in discussion, knew many historical precedents, and could detail and recall all clansmen and figures since the Tang house.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in discussion, knew many historical precedents, and could detail and recall all clansmen and figures since the Tang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 酷好吟詠，每對客論詩，終日忘倦。

translations.literal: He ardently loved chanting and composition; whenever facing guests in discussion of poetry he forgot fatigue for a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: He ardently loved chanting and composition; whenever facing guests in discussion of poetry he forgot fatigue for a whole day.

sentences.zh: 既沒，有集二十卷留於家，上令夏侯嶠取之以進。

translations.literal: After his death a collected works of twenty juan remained in his household; the sovereign ordered Xiahou Qiao to fetch it and present it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death a collected works of twenty juan remained in his household; the emperor ordered Xiahou Qiao to fetch it and present it.

sentences.zh: 徽之無子。

translations.literal: Huizhi had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi had no sons.

sentences.zh: 後徽之妻王卒，及葬，復以緡帛賜其家。

translations.literal: Later Huizhi's wife Wang died; upon her burial silk and cash were again granted to the family.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huizhi's wife Wang died; upon her burial silk and cash were again granted to the family.

sentences.zh: 澈，字晏如，徽之宗人也，世家建陽。

translations.literal: Che, style name Yanru, was a clansman of Huizhi; his family for generations had been based in Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Che, courtesy name Yanru, was a clansman of Huizhi; his family for generations had been based in Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 父思進，晉天福中北渡海，因家於青州之北海，累佐使幕。

translations.literal: His father Sijin, during the Tianfu era of Jin crossed north by sea and settled the family in Beihai in Qing Prefecture; he repeatedly served as aide on commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sijin, during the Tianfu era of Jin crossed north by sea and settled the family in Beihai in Qing Prefecture; he repeatedly served as aide on commissioners' staffs.

sentences.zh: 澈幼聰警，七歲讀《春秋左氏傳》，即曉大義。

translations.literal: Che from youth was keen and alert; at seven reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, he immediately grasped its broad meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Che from youth was keen and alert; at seven, reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, he immediately grasped its broad meaning.

sentences.zh: 周宰相李穀召令默誦，一無遺誤，穀甚異之。

translations.literal: Zhou chief minister Li Gu summoned him and ordered him to recite from memory—without a single omission or error; Li was greatly struck.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou chief minister Li Gu summoned him and ordered him to recite from memory—without a single omission or error; Li was greatly struck.

sentences.zh: 年十六，思進為鎮趙從事，會昭慶令缺，使府命澈假其任。

translations.literal: At age sixteen Sijin was an aide on the Zhen Prefecture staff; when the magistrate of Zhaoqing fell vacant, the commissioner's office ordered Che to act in the post.
translations.idiomatic: At age sixteen Sijin was an aide on the Zhen Prefecture staff; when the magistrate of Zhaoqing fell vacant, the commissioner's office ordered Che to act in the post.

sentences.zh: 時河決鄰郡，府督役甚急。

translations.literal: At the time a river burst its banks in a neighboring prefecture and the commissioner's office pressed corvée labor with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a river burst its banks in a neighboring prefecture and the commissioner's office pressed corvée labor with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 澈部徒數千，徑大澤中，多蘆葦，令采刈為筏，順流而下。

translations.literal: Che directed several thousand corvée laborers through a great marsh rich in reeds and ordered them to cut and harvest reeds to make rafts and float downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Che directed several thousand corvée laborers through a great marsh rich in reeds and ordered them to cut and harvest reeds to make rafts and float downstream.

sentences.zh: 既至，執事者訝以後期，俄而葦筏繼至，駭而問之，澈以狀對，乃更嗟賞。

translations.literal: When he arrived, those in charge were astonished at his lateness; but soon the reed rafts came in succession; startled they inquired, and Che answered with the facts—they then admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, those in charge were astonished at his lateness; but soon the reed rafts came in succession; startled, they inquired, and Che answered with the facts—they then admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，舉進士，時竇儀典貢部，謂澈文詞敏速，可當書檄之任。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong he passed the jinshi examination; Dou Yi then presided over the examination bureau and said Che's literary style was swift and able—fit for dispatch-writing duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianlong he passed the jinshi examination; Dou Yi then presided over the examination bureau and said Che's literary style was swift and able—fit for dispatch-writing duties.

sentences.zh: 調補河內主簿，再遷青州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Assigned as recorder of Henei, he was again promoted to revenue section aide of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as recorder of Henei, he was again promoted to revenue section aide of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知州張全操多不法，澈鞫獄平允，無所阿畏。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Quancao committed many illegal acts; Che tried cases with fair judgment and showed no partial favor or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Quancao committed many illegal acts; Che tried cases with fair judgment and showed no partial favor or fear.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其名，召試禁中，改著作佐郎，出知渠州。

translations.literal: Taizu knew his name, summoned him for examination within the palace, transferred him to assistant compiler, and sent him out as prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu knew his name, summoned him for examination within the palace, transferred him to assistant compiler, and sent him out as prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 江南平，改通判虔州，令就大將曹彬分兵以行。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified he was changed to supervisory commissioner of Qian Prefecture and ordered to join the great general Cao Bin with a division of troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan was pacified he was changed to supervisory commissioner of Qian Prefecture and ordered to join the great general Cao Bin with a division of troops.

sentences.zh: 既入境，偽帥郭再興擁兵自固，澈單騎直趨其壘，諭以朝廷威信，再興即奉符以代。

translations.literal: Once he entered the territory, the false commander Guo Zaixing held troops and fortified himself; Che alone on horseback rode straight to his camp, admonished him with the court's authority and prestige, and Zaixing at once surrendered his seal for replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the territory, the false commander Guo Zaixing held troops and fortified himself; Che alone on horseback rode straight to his camp, admonished him with the court's authority and prestige, and Zaixing at once surrendered his seal for replacement.

sentences.zh: 澈悉料城中軍士之勇壯者，凡五百人為一綱，部送京師。

translations.literal: Che fully assessed the brave and strong soldiers in the city, grouped them five hundred per unit, and escorted them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Che fully assessed the brave and strong soldiers in the city, grouped them five hundred per unit, and escorted them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 土豪黎、羅二姓，聚眾依山謀亂，澈率兵平之，擒二豪，械送闕下。

translations.literal: Local magnates of the Li and Luo clans gathered crowds in the mountains plotting rebellion; Che led troops and pacified them, captured the two magnates, and sent them in fetters to court.
translations.idiomatic: Local magnates of the Li and Luo clans gathered crowds in the mountains plotting rebellion; Che led troops and pacified them, captured the two magnates, and sent them in fetters to court.

sentences.zh: 遷右贊善大夫、知淄州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Supporter Grandee and prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Supporter Grandee and prefect of Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事親以孝聞，求便侍養，徙同判青州。

translations.literal: Renowned for filial service to parents, he requested a convenient post to attend them and was moved to co-commissioner of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for filial service to parents, he requested a convenient post to attend them and was moved to co-commissioner of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三遷祠部員外郎，復知淄州，又知舒州，累轉祠部郎中。

translations.literal: Three times promoted to outer bureau director of the Ministry of Rites; again prefect of Zi, then of Shu; cumulatively transferred to bureau director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Three times promoted to outer bureau director of the Ministry of Rites; again prefect of Zi, then of Shu; cumulatively transferred to bureau director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，遴選王府僚佐，以澈為雍王府記室參軍，賜金紫，加度支郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, selecting staff for the princely establishment, Che was made registrar of the Yong Prince's household, granted gold-purple insignia, and given the added post of bureau director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping, selecting staff for the princely establishment, Che was made registrar of the Yong Prince's household, granted gold-and-purple insignia, and given the added post of bureau director of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 景德初，車駕幸澶淵，王為東京留守，澈遷兵部郎中，充留守判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, when the imperial carriage visited Chanyuan, the prince remained in charge at the Eastern Capital; Che was moved to bureau director of the Ministry of War and appointed judge of the garrison staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde, when the imperial carriage visited Chanyuan, the prince remained in charge at the Eastern Capital; Che was moved to bureau director of the Ministry of War and appointed judge of the garrison staff.

sentences.zh: 軍巡囚逸，王驚而感疾，及薨，又得閨門殘忍之狀，坐輔導不善免官。

translations.literal: A military patrol prisoner escaped; the prince was alarmed and fell ill; when he died, evidence also emerged of cruel conduct within the inner quarters; Che was punished for poor guidance and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: A military patrol prisoner escaped; the prince was alarmed and fell ill; when he died, evidence also emerged of cruel conduct within the inner quarters; Che was punished for poor guidance and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起為祠部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as bureau director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as bureau director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子巒，淳化進士，職方員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Luan, jinshi of the Chunhua era, outer bureau director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luan, a jinshi of the Chunhua era, served as outer bureau director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 呂文仲

translations.literal: Lü Wenshong
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenshong

sentences.zh: 呂文仲，字子臧，歙州新安人。

translations.literal: Lü Wenshong, style name Zizang, was a native of Xin'an in She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenshong, courtesy name Zizang, was from Xin'an in She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父裕，偽唐歙州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Yu was recorder of She Prefecture under the false Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was recorder of She Prefecture under the false Tang.

sentences.zh: 文仲在江左，舉進士，調補臨川尉，再遷大理評事，掌宗室書奏。

translations.literal: Wenshong in the lands east of the Yangtze passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as magistrate of Linchuan, again promoted to appraiser of the Court of Judicial Review, and directed memorials of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshong in the lands east of the Yangtze passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as magistrate of Linchuan, again promoted to appraiser of the Court of Judicial Review, and directed memorials of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 入朝，授太常寺太祝，稍遷少府監丞。

translations.literal: Entering court service he was appointed Director of Solemnity in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and gradually promoted to assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: Entering court service he was appointed Director of Solemnity in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and gradually promoted to assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 預修太平《御覽》、《廣記》、《文苑英華》，改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Taiping Imperial Digest, Extensive Record, and Wen yuan ying hua, and was transferred to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He participated in compiling the Taiping Imperial Digest, Extensive Record, and Wen yuan ying hua, and was transferred to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，上每御便殿觀古碑刻，輒召文仲與舒雅、杜鎬、吳淑讀之。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo whenever the sovereign visited the Informal Hall to view ancient stelae and inscriptions, he would summon Wenshong with Shu Ya, Du Gao, and Wu Shu to read them.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo whenever the emperor visited the Informal Hall to view ancient stelae and inscriptions, he would summon Wenshong with Shu Ya, Du Gao, and Wu Shu to read them.

sentences.zh: 嘗令文仲讀《文選》，繼又令讀《江海賦》，皆有賜齎。

translations.literal: Once he ordered Wenshong to read the Wen xuan; afterward ordered him to read the Jianghai fu—both times gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ordered Wenshong to read the Wen xuan; afterward ordered him to read the Jianghai fu—both times gifts were granted.

sentences.zh: 以本官充翰林侍讀，寓直御書院，與侍書王著更宿。

translations.literal: With his existing office he served as Hanlin Attendant Reader, lodged on duty at the Imperial Calligraphy Academy, and alternated night watches with calligraphy attendant Wang Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: With his existing office he served as Hanlin Attendant Reader, lodged on duty at the Imperial Calligraphy Academy, and alternated night watches with calligraphy attendant Wang Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 時書學葛湍亦直禁中，太宗暇日，每從容問文仲以書史、著以筆法、湍以字學。

translations.literal: At the time calligraphy student Ge Tuan also served within the palace; on Emperor Taizong's leisure days he would at ease question Wenshong on books and history, Zhuo on brush technique, and Tuan on character study.
translations.idiomatic: At the time calligraphy student Ge Tuan also served within the palace; on Emperor Taizong's leisure days he would at ease question Wenshong on books and history, Zhuo on brush technique, and Tuan on character study.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，文仲遷著作佐郎，副王著使高麗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi Wenshong was promoted to assistant compiler and served as deputy to Wang Zhuo on the mission to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi Wenshong was promoted to assistant compiler and served as deputy to Wang Zhuo on the mission to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 復命改左正言，巡撫福建。

translations.literal: Upon return from the mission he was made Left Rectifier and toured and pacified Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Upon return from the mission he was made Left Rectifier and toured and pacified Fujian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賜金紫，加左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was granted gold-purple insignia and given the added post of Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was granted gold-and-purple insignia and given the added post of Left Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，與陳堯叟並兼關西巡撫使。

translations.literal: During Chunhua he and Chen Yaosou together concurrently served as touring commissioners of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he and Chen Yaosou together concurrently served as touring commissioners of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 時內品方保吉專幹榷酤，威制郡縣。

translations.literal: At the time the inner palace attendant Fang Baoji exclusively managed the salt-and-wine monopoly and held counties and prefectures in the grip of his authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the inner palace attendant Fang Baoji exclusively managed the salt-and-wine monopoly and held counties and prefectures in the grip of his authority.

sentences.zh: 民疲吏擾，變易舊法，訟其掊克者甚眾。

translations.literal: The people were exhausted and officials harassed; he changed the old regulations, and lawsuits accusing him of extortion were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The people were exhausted and officials harassed; he changed the old regulations, and lawsuits accusing him of extortion were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 文仲等具奏其實，太宗怒甚。

translations.literal: Wenshong and the others fully memorialized the facts; Emperor Taizong was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshong and the others fully memorialized the facts; Emperor Taizong was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 亟召保吉，將劾之，反為保吉所訟，下御史驗問。

translations.literal: He quickly summoned Baoji intending to impeach him, but instead was sued by Baoji and the case was sent to the censorate for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He quickly summoned Baoji intending to impeach him, but instead was sued by Baoji and the case was sent to the censorate for investigation.

sentences.zh: 文仲所坐皆細事，而素巽懦，且恥與保吉辨對，因自誣伏，遂罷職。

translations.literal: The offenses Wenshong was charged with were all petty matters; but he was by nature submissive and timid, and moreover ashamed to argue face to face with Baoji, so he falsely confessed on his own and was thereupon dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The offenses Wenshong was charged with were all petty matters; but he was by nature submissive and timid, and moreover ashamed to argue face to face with Baoji, so he falsely confessed on his own and was thereupon dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 既而太宗知其由，復令直秘閣；

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Taizong learned the reason and again ordered him to serve at the Secretariat Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Taizong learned the truth of the matter and again appointed him to serve at the Secretariat Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 逾月，再為侍讀。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he again became attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was again made attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 一日，召於崇政殿，讀上草書經史故實數十軸，詔模刻於石。

translations.literal: One day he was summoned to Chongzheng Hall; he read aloud to the emperor several dozen scrolls of cursive-script historical anecdotes from the classics and histories, and an edict ordered them carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was summoned to Chongzheng Hall, where he read aloud to the emperor several dozen scrolls of cursive historical anecdotes drawn from the classics; an edict then ordered the texts carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人、兵部員外郎、同判吏部銓，知銀臺通進封駁司、審官院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to diarist of the palace, vice director of the Ministry of War, concurrent supervisor of the Ministry of Personnel's selection office, and director of the Yintai Directorate for Memorial Submission and Seal Verification and the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace diarist and vice director of the Ministry of War, concurrently supervised the Ministry of Personnel's selection office, and directed the Yintai Directorate for Memorial Submission and Seal Verification and the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，拜工部郎中，充翰林侍讀學士，受詔集太宗歌詩為三十卷，詔書加獎，又知審刑院。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he was appointed director of the Ministry of Works, served as Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician, received an edict to compile Emperor Taizong's song-poems into thirty scrolls, received commendation in an edict, and also directed the Bureau for Review of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was appointed director of the Ministry of Works and Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician, tasked by imperial edict to compile Emperor Taizong's lyric poems into thirty scrolls; the court issued a commendation, and he also took charge of the Bureau for Review of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 六年，授御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 景德中，鞫曹州姦民趙諫獄。

translations.literal: During the Jingde era he investigated the case of the wicked commoner Zhao Jian of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era he tried the case of Zhao Jian, a scoundrel from Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 諫多與士大夫交遊，內出姓名七十餘人，令悉窮治。

translations.literal: Jian had extensive contacts among literati and officials; from the palace a list of more than seventy names was issued, ordering that all be thoroughly prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had extensive ties to literati and officials; the court produced a list of more than seventy names from within and ordered them all pursued to the end.

sentences.zh: 文仲請對，言逮捕者眾，或在外郡，苟悉索之，慮動人聽。

translations.literal: Wenshong requested an audience and said that those to be arrested were many, some in distant prefectures; if all were sought out, he feared it would alarm the public.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshong requested an audience, arguing that many were marked for arrest, some in distant prefectures, and that a sweeping roundup would alarm the country.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿執憲，當嫉惡如仇，豈公行黨庇邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You enforce the law—you should hate evil as one hates a foe; how could you openly shield a faction?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You hold the scales of justice. You should hate wickedness as you would a mortal enemy—would you openly protect a clique instead?"

sentences.zh: 」文仲頓首曰：「中司之職，非徒繩糾愆違，亦當顧國家大體。

translations.literal: Wenshong kowtowed and said: "The duty of the central censorate is not merely to bind and punish transgressions; one must also consider the larger interests of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshong kowtowed and said, "The censorate exists not only to punish wrongdoing—it must also weigh the larger interests of the realm."

sentences.zh: 今縱七十人悉得姦狀，以陛下之慈仁，必不盡戮，不過廢棄而已。

translations.literal: Now even if all seventy are found guilty, given Your Majesty's compassionate benevolence they surely would not all be executed—at most they would be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Even if all seventy were proved guilty, Your Majesty's mercy would surely spare their lives—they would at worst be discarded from office.

sentences.zh: 但籍其名，更察其為人，置於冗散，或舉選對揚之日擯斥之，未為晚也。

translations.literal: It is enough to register their names, further examine their conduct, place them in idle posts, or at the time of the civil-service examinations and court audiences exclude them—it would not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Register their names, watch their conduct, assign them to idle posts, or exclude them when examinations and imperial audiences come round—that would be time enough.

sentences.zh: 」上從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷工部侍郎，復為翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Works and again became Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Works and again made Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.

sentences.zh: 文仲久居禁近，頗周密兢慎。

translations.literal: Wenshong had long served near the forbidden precincts and was quite thorough and cautious in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshong had long served within the inner palace and was meticulous and cautious in all he did.

sentences.zh: 一日早朝，暴得風疾，請告逾百日，詔續其奉。

translations.literal: One day at the morning audience he suddenly suffered a wind ailment; he requested leave for more than a hundred days, and an edict continued his salary.
translations.idiomatic: One morning at court he was suddenly struck by paralysis; he took leave for more than a hundred days, and the emperor ordered his salary continued.

sentences.zh: 明年，改刑部侍郎，充集賢院學士，未幾卒，錄其子永為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to vice director of the Ministry of Justice, served as academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and before long died; his son Yong was granted the post of ceremonial attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became vice director of the Ministry of Justice and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; he died shortly after, and his son Yong was granted the rank of ceremonial attendant.

sentences.zh: 文仲富詞學，器韻淹雅。

translations.literal: Wenshong was rich in literary learning; his bearing and tone were refined and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshong was deeply learned in letters, with a refined and graceful bearing.

sentences.zh: 其使高麗也，善於應對，清淨無所求，遠俗悅之。

translations.literal: When he served as envoy to Goryeo, he was adept at repartee, pure and free of requests; the distant people were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy to Goryeo he answered every challenge with grace, asked for nothing, and won over a foreign court.

sentences.zh: 後有使高麗者，必詢其出處。

translations.literal: Later envoys to Goryeo always inquired about his origins.
translations.idiomatic: Later envoys to Goryeo were invariably asked where he had come from.

sentences.zh: 然性頗齷齪，不為時論所許。

translations.literal: Yet his character was rather narrow and petty, and he was not approved by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was petty and narrow-minded, and won little esteem among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 王著，字知微，文仲同時人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhuo, style name Zhiwei, was a contemporary of Wenshong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo, courtesy name Zhiwei, lived in the same era as Wenshong.

sentences.zh: 自言唐相石泉公方慶之後，世家京兆渭南。

translations.literal: He claimed to be a descendant of Tang chancellor the Duke of Shiquan, Fang Qing; his family had long resided in Weinan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from the Tang chancellor Fang Qing, Duke of Shiquan, from a long-established family in Weinan, near the capital.

sentences.zh: 祖賁，廣明中從僖宗入蜀，遂為成都人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ben, during the Guangming era followed Emperor Xizong into Shu, and thereafter became a man of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ben followed Emperor Xizong into Shu during the Guangming era and settled in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 賁仕王建，為雅州刺史。

translations.literal: Ben served Wang Jian as prefect of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ben served Wang Jian as prefect of Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父景瓌，萬州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Jinggui served as vice governor of Wan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinggui was vice governor of Wan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 著，偽蜀明經及第，歷平泉、百丈、永康主簿。

translations.literal: Zhuo passed the Mingjing examination in the puppet Shu state and successively served as registrar of Pingquan, Baizhang, and Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo passed the classics examination in Later Shu and served successively as registrar at Pingquan, Baizhang, and Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 蜀平赴闕，授隆平主簿，凡十一年不代。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he went to court and was appointed registrar of Longping; for eleven years he received no replacement.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he presented himself at court and was given the post of registrar at Longping, which he held for eleven years without relief.

sentences.zh: 著善攻書，筆跡甚媚，頗有家法。

translations.literal: Zhuo excelled at calligraphy; his brush traces were very graceful and showed a distinct family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was a master of calligraphy—his hand was graceful and bore the mark of a true family tradition.

sentences.zh: 太宗以字書訛舛，欲令學士刪定，少通習者。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, finding that character dictionaries were erroneous and corrupt, wished to have academicians revise them, but few were versed in the subject.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong found the standard dictionaries riddled with errors and wished to have court scholars revise them, but few had the expertise.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，轉運使侯陟以著名聞，改衛寺丞、史館祗候，委以詳定篇韻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo Transport Commissioner Hou Zhi reported his fame for calligraphy; he was changed to assistant director of the Guard Office and attendant at the Historiography Institute, entrusted with revising the rhyme dictionary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, Transport Commissioner Hou Zhi brought Zhuo's reputation to the court's attention; he was made assistant director of the Guard Office and attendant at the Historiography Institute and charged with revising the rhyme dictionary.

sentences.zh: 六年，召見，賜緋，加著作佐郎、翰林侍書與侍讀，更直於御書院。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned for an audience, granted crimson robes, given the added posts of assistant compiler and Hanlin Attendant Calligrapher and Reader, and alternated duty at the Imperial Calligraphy Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was summoned to audience, granted crimson robes, and given the titles of assistant compiler, Hanlin Attendant Calligrapher and Reader, with rotating duty at the Imperial Calligraphy Academy.

sentences.zh: 太宗聽政之暇，嘗以觀書及筆法為意，諸家字體，洞臻精妙。

translations.literal: In his leisure from hearing affairs Emperor Taizong often took pleasure in reading books and brush technique; the styles of every school he mastered to exquisite perfection.
translations.idiomatic: In his moments away from governance Taizong devoted himself to reading and the art of the brush, mastering every school of calligraphy to exquisite perfection.

sentences.zh: 嘗令中使王仁睿持御劄示著，著曰：「未盡善也。

translations.literal: He once had palace emissary Wang Renrui bring an imperial draft to show Zhuo; Zhuo said: "It is not yet perfect."
translations.idiomatic: Once he had the palace emissary Wang Renrui show Zhuo an imperial draft. Zhuo said, "This is not yet perfect."

sentences.zh: 」太宗臨學益勤，又以示著，著答如前。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong practiced with increased diligence; he again showed it to Zhuo, and Zhuo answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong redoubled his practice and showed the work to Zhuo again; Zhuo gave the same answer.

sentences.zh: 仁睿詰其故，著曰：「帝王始攻書，或驟稱善，則不復留心矣。

translations.literal: Renrui pressed him for the reason; Zhuo said: "When a ruler first takes up calligraphy, if one suddenly praises it as good, he will no longer pay heed."
translations.idiomatic: Renrui pressed him for an explanation. Zhuo said, "When an emperor first takes up the brush, sudden praise only teaches him to stop caring."

sentences.zh: 」久之，復以示著。

translations.literal: After a long while he again showed it to Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Much later he showed it to Zhuo once more.

sentences.zh: 著曰：「功已至矣，非臣所能及。

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "The achievement has reached its summit; it is beyond what your subject can attain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo said, "The mastery is complete—your servant could never reach it."

sentences.zh: 」其後真宗嘗對宰相語其事，且嘉著之善於規益，於侍書待詔中亦無其比。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Zhenzong once spoke of the affair to his chief ministers and praised Zhuo's skill at admonition and benefit; among attendant calligraphers and awaiting-edict officials there was none to compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Zhenzong told his chief ministers the story and praised Zhuo's gift for honest counsel; among the court calligraphers none compared with him.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，遷左拾遺，使高麗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was transferred to Left Reminder and sent as envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was promoted to Left Reminder and dispatched as envoy to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was given the added post of palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era he was additionally made palace censor.

sentences.zh: 二年，與文仲同賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the second year he and Wenshong together were granted gold-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he and Wenshong were together granted gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，特加賵賜，錄其子嗣復為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: The next year he died; special funeral gifts were added, and his son Sifu was granted the post of ceremonial attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year; the court granted special funeral gifts and enfeoffed his son Sifu as ceremonial attendant.

sentences.zh: 呂祐之

translations.literal: Lu Youzhi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youzhi

sentences.zh: 呂祐之，字元吉，濟州鉅野人。

translations.literal: Lu Youzhi, style name Yuanji, was a native of Juye in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youzhi, courtesy name Yuanji, was from Juye in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父文賛，本州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Wenzan served as registrar of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenzan was registrar of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祐之，太平興國初，舉進士，解褐大理評事、通判洋州。

translations.literal: Youzhi, at the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, passed the jinshi examination; he began his career as judge of the Court of Judicial Review and administrative assistant of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi passed the jinshi examination at the opening of Taiping Xingguo and took his first post as judge of the Court of Judicial Review and deputy prefect of Yang.

sentences.zh: 改右贊善大夫，出為泰寧軍節度判官，移天雄軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Supporter Grandee, sent out as military aide to the military commissioner of Taining Army, then transferred to Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Supporter Grandee, then served as staff officer to the military commissioner of Taining and later transferred to Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 召拜殿中侍御史，決獄西蜀。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed palace censor, and adjudicated cases in western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was made palace censor and sent to try cases in western Shu.

sentences.zh: 還知貝州，換右補闕、直史館、同判吏部南曹，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: Upon return he governed Bei Prefecture, then was changed to Right Supplementation Reminder, served directly at the Historiography Institute, concurrently supervised the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, and was transferred to palace diarist.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he governed Bei Prefecture, then became Right Supplementation Reminder with direct appointment to the Historiography Institute, concurrent supervisor of the Ministry of Personnel's southern bureau, and finally palace diarist.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，副呂端使高麗，假內庫錢五十萬以辦裝。

translations.literal: During Duangong he served as deputy to Lu Duan on the Goryeo mission, borrowing five hundred thousand in cash from the inner treasury for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: During Duangong he served under Lu Duan as deputy envoy to Goryeo, borrowing five hundred thousand cash from the inner treasury for his equipage.

sentences.zh: 還，遇風濤，舟欲覆，祐之悉取所得貨沉之，即止。

translations.literal: On the return voyage they met wind and waves; the boat was about to capsize; Youzhi took all the goods he had obtained and sank them, and then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On the return voyage a storm nearly capsized the ship; Youzhi threw all his goods overboard, and the tempest abated.

sentences.zh: 復獻《海外覃皇澤詩》十九首，太宗嘉之，仍蠲其所貸。

translations.literal: He also presented "Nineteen Poems on the Emperor's Grace Spreading Overseas"; Emperor Taizong commended him and furthermore remitted the loan.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented nineteen poems titled "The Emperor's Grace Spreading Overseas"; Taizong praised them and cancelled his debt.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，判戶部勾院，會分備三館職，以祐之與趙昂、安德裕並直昭文館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he presided over the Household Ministry audit office; when the three academies' posts were divided and filled, Youzhi with Zhao Ang and An Deyu together served directly at the Zhaowen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chunhua he headed the Household Ministry audit office; when the three academies were staffed anew, he was posted with Zhao Ang and An Deyu to the Zhaowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官知制誥，賜金紫，同知貢舉。

translations.literal: Before long, with his existing office he was made drafter of edicts, granted gold-purple insignia, and served concurrently as chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made edict drafter while retaining his rank, granted gold-and-purple insignia, and appointed concurrent chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 有東野日宣者，祐之以妻族嘗薦舉之，坐鞫獄陳州不實，貶官，祐之亦降授殿中丞，再直史館。

translations.literal: There was one Dongye Rixuan whom Youzhi had once recommended as a wife's kinsman; tried for a false case at Chen Prefecture, he was demoted; Youzhi too was reduced to palace secretary and again served directly at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had once recommended a wife's kinsman, Dongye Rixuan; when Rixuan was tried at Chen Prefecture for a false case and demoted, Youzhi was lowered to palace secretary and returned to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long he again served as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made edict drafter.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗閱班簿，擇近臣舉官，睹祐之姓名，宰相因言其前坐舉無狀。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once reviewed the roster, selecting close ministers to recommend officials; seeing Youzhi's name, the chief minister thereupon spoke of his earlier offense of baseless recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Taizong reviewed the roster to choose ministers who would recommend officials, he came upon Youzhi's name; the chief minister noted his earlier offense of recommending an unworthy man.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此正可令贖過矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is exactly the sort who should be allowed to redeem past faults."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is exactly the sort of case where a man should be allowed to redeem his past mistake."

sentences.zh: 」即取祐之焉。

translations.literal: He immediately selected Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He chose Youzhi on the spot.

sentences.zh: 至道初，拜右諫議大夫，賜金紫，知審官院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee, granted gold-purple insignia, and directed the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhidao he was made Right Remonstrance Grandee, granted gold-and-purple insignia, and put in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 出知襄州，徙壽州。

translations.literal: He was sent out to govern Xiang Prefecture, then transferred to Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Xiang Prefecture, then transferred to Shou.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，轉給事中，復知襄州，移升州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to supervising censor, again governed Xiang Prefecture, then moved to Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong came to the throne, Youzhi was made supervising censor, again governed Xiang, and was then transferred to Sheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，又典襄陽。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again administered Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was again put in charge of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 歸，掌吏部選事，知通進、銀臺司，與呂文仲並拜工部侍郎、翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Upon return he managed selection affairs at the Ministry of Personnel, directed the Directorate for Memorial Submission and the Yintai Directorate, and with Lu Wenzhong together was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Works and Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he took charge of Ministry of Personnel selections, directed the memorial submission and Yintai offices, and was jointly elevated with Lu Wenzhong to vice director of the Ministry of Works and Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.

sentences.zh: 自置侍讀、侍講，甚艱其選，至是裁七人。

translations.literal: Since establishing the posts of attendant reader and attendant expositor, selection had been very difficult; by this time there were only seven.
translations.idiomatic: Since the creation of the attendant reader and expositor posts, selection had been arduous—only seven men had ever held them.

sentences.zh: 祐之第其名氏，刻石於秘閣。

translations.literal: Youzhi ranked their names and had them carved in stone at the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi ordered their names inscribed on stone in the Secretariat Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 祐之純謹長者，不喜趨競，所至無顯譽，備顧問，不能有所啟發。

translations.literal: Youzhi was a pure, prudent elder; he did not care for scrambling for advancement; wherever he went he won no conspicuous renown; though present for counsel, he could offer no inspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was a sincere and cautious man of steady character who shunned the scramble for advancement; he won no great fame wherever he served, and though he stood among the emperor's advisers, he seldom stirred fresh insight.

sentences.zh: 會文仲以疾罷近職，祐之亦出為集賢院學士，仍並遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Wenshong was removed from proximity on account of illness, Youzhi too was sent out as academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and both were concurrently transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenshong fell ill and left his inner-court post, Youzhi too was posted to the Hall of Assembled Worthies; both men were concurrently promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Jingde, at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 潘慎修

translations.literal: Pan Shenxiu
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shenxiu

sentences.zh: 潘慎修，字成德，泉州莆田縣人。

translations.literal: Pan Shenxiu, style name Chengde, was a native of Putian County in Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shenxiu, courtesy name Chengde, was from Putian County in Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父承祐，仕閩，後歸江南，仕李景，至刑部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: His father Chengyou served Min, later returned to Jiangnan, served Li Jing, and retired as minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengyou had served Min, then Jiangnan under Li Jing, retiring as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 慎修少以父任為秘書省正字，累遷至水部郎中兼起居舍人。

translations.literal: Shenxiu in youth entered office through his father's privilege as corrector of the Secretariat, and was incrementally promoted to director of the Waterworks Ministry concurrently serving as palace diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu entered government young through his father's privilege as a corrector in the Secretariat, rising to director of the Waterworks Ministry while also serving as palace diarist.

sentences.zh: 開寶末，王師征江南，李煜遣隨其弟從鎰入貢買宴錢，求緩兵。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaibao the imperial army attacked Jiangnan; Li Yu sent him to accompany his younger brother Congyi to present tribute and "banquet money," seeking to delay the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaibao, as Song armies marched on Jiangnan, Li Yu sent Shenxiu with his brother Congyi to court with tribute and "banquet funds," hoping to stall the invasion.

sentences.zh: 留館懷信驛。

translations.literal: They lodged at the Huaixin post station.
translations.idiomatic: They were lodged at the Huaixin post station.

sentences.zh: 旦夕捷書至，邸吏督從鎰入賀。

translations.literal: Morning and evening victory reports arrived; hostel clerks urged Congyi to enter and offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day victory dispatches arrived, and the hostel clerks pressed Congyi to go in and offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 慎修以為國且亡，當待罪，何賀也？

translations.literal: Shenxiu considered that the state was about to perish—one should await punishment; why congratulate?
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu protested: the realm was about to fall—this was a time for repentance, not congratulations.

sentences.zh: 自是每群臣稱賀，從鎰即奉表請罪。

translations.literal: Thereafter whenever the court ministers offered congratulations, Congyi would submit a memorial asking forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the court celebrated a victory, Congyi submitted a memorial begging forgiveness instead.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其得禮，遣中使慰諭，供帳牢餼悉加優給。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu commended his propriety, sent a palace emissary to console and instruct him, and added generous provision to his lodging and rations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu praised his grasp of propriety, sent a palace envoy to commend him, and saw that his lodgings and provisions were generously supplied.

sentences.zh: 煜歸朝，以慎修為太子右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: When Yu came to court, Shenxiu was made Right Supporter Grandee of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu surrendered and came to court, Shenxiu was made Right Supporter Grandee to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 煜表求慎修掌記室，許之。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized requesting Shenxiu to manage his secretariat; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu petitioned to keep Shenxiu as chief of his secretariat, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 煜卒，改太常博士。

translations.literal: When Yu died, he was changed to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Yu died, he was reassigned as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歷膳部、倉部、考功三員外，通判壽州，知開封縣，又知湖、梓二州。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice director of the Commissariat, Granary, and Merit ministries; administrative assistant of Shou Prefecture; magistrate of Kaifeng County; and governor of Hu and Zi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice director in the Commissariat, Granary, and Merit ministries, as deputy prefect of Shou, as magistrate of Kaifeng County, and as prefect of Hu and Zi.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，秘書監李至薦之，命以本官知直秘閣。

translations.literal: During Chunhua Secretariat Director Li Zhi recommended him; he was ordered with his existing office to serve as director on duty at the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua, Secretariat Director Li Zhi recommended him, and he was appointed to direct duty at the Secretariat Pavilion while retaining his rank.

sentences.zh: 慎修善弈棋，太宗屢召對弈，因作《棋說》以獻。

translations.literal: Shenxiu excelled at go; Emperor Taizong repeatedly summoned him to play, and he therefore composed "An Essay on Go" and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu was an expert at go; Taizong often summoned him to play, and Shenxiu composed "An Essay on Go" and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 大抵謂：「棋之道在乎恬默，而取舍為急。

translations.literal: It largely stated: "The way of go lies in stillness and silence, yet deciding what to take and what to leave is urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Its gist was this: "The art of go rests on stillness and restraint, yet knowing what to seize and what to surrender is everything."

sentences.zh: 仁則能全，義則能守，禮則能變，智則能兼，信則能克。

translations.literal: With benevolence one can preserve wholeness; with righteousness one can hold firm; with ritual one can change; with wisdom one can embrace all; with trustworthiness one can overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence preserves wholeness; righteousness holds the line; ritual enables adaptation; wisdom embraces every possibility; trustworthiness achieves victory.

sentences.zh: 君子知斯五者，庶幾可以言棋矣。

translations.literal: If a noble man knows these five, he may perhaps speak of go.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman who understands these five virtues may be said to understand go.

sentences.zh: 」因舉十要以明其義，太宗覽而稱善。

translations.literal: He then raised ten key points to clarify their meaning; Emperor Taizong read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out ten principles to illustrate their meaning; Taizong read the essay and commended it.

sentences.zh: 俄與直昭文館韓援使淮南巡撫，累遷倉部、考功二部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long, with Hanlin attendant at the Zhaowen Pavilion Han Yuan he toured and pacified Huainan; he was incrementally promoted to director of the Granary and Merit ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was sent with Han Yuan of the Zhaowen Pavilion to tour and pacify Huainan, and was promoted in turn to director of the Granary and Merit ministries.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，又副邢昺為兩浙巡撫使，俄同修起居注。

translations.literal: During Xianping he again served as deputy to Xing Bing as touring commissioner of the two Zhe circuits; before long he concurrently compiled the court diary.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping he served under Xing Bing as deputy commissioner for the two Zhe circuits, and soon afterward was made compiler of the court diary.

sentences.zh: 景德初，上言衰老，求外任。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he memorialized that he was aged and sought an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingde he petitioned that age had weakened him and asked for a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 真宗以儒雅宜留秘府，止聽解記注之職。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, considering his cultured refinement suited to remaining in the secret archives, only permitted him to relinquish the diary-compiler post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong judged his erudition too valuable for the secretariat to lose and allowed him only to step down from compiling the court diary.

sentences.zh: 數月，擢為右諫議大夫、翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: After several months he was elevated to Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was elevated to Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.

sentences.zh: 從幸澶州，遘寒疾，詔令肩輿先歸。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on the visit to Chanzhou, he contracted a cold ailment; an edict ordered him carried in a sedan chair to return first.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the emperor to Chanzhou he fell ill with a chill; the emperor ordered him carried home in a sedan ahead of the retinue.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year in the first month, at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賻錢二十萬，絹一百匹。

translations.literal: Gratuities of money two hundred thousand, silk one hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted two hundred thousand strings in funeral gratuities and one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 慎修疾雖亟，精爽不亂，託陳彭年草遺奏，不為諸子干澤，但以主恩未報為恨。

translations.literal: Shenxiu though his illness was urgent, his spirit and clarity were not disorderly; he entrusted Chen Pengnian to draft his final memorial, did not seek benefits from the emperor for his sons, but took as regret that the sovereign's grace had not been repaid.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shenxiu's illness was grave, his mind remained clear. He had Chen Pengnian draft his final memorial, seeking no favors for his sons—only lamenting that he had not yet repaid the emperor's grace.

sentences.zh: 上憫之，錄其子汝士為大理評事，汝礪為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him, enrolled his son Rushi as judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, and Ruli as ceremonial attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and appointed his son Rushi as judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and Ruli as ceremonial attendant.

sentences.zh: 令有司給舟載其柩歸洪州。

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to provide a boat to carry his coffin back to Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the proper authorities to provide a boat to convey the coffin back to Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 慎修風度醞藉，博涉文史，多讀道書，善清談。

translations.literal: Shenxiu in bearing was cultured and self-restrained, broadly versed in literature and history, read many Daoist books, and excelled at pure conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu cultivated an elegant, reserved manner. He ranged widely through literature and history, read extensively in Daoist texts, and excelled at refined conversation.

sentences.zh: 先是，江南舊臣多言李煜暗懦，事多過實。

translations.literal: Previously, old ministers of Jiangnan often said Li Yu was dim and weak, and matters were mostly exaggerated beyond truth.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, former ministers of Jiangnan had often called Li Yu dim-witted and weak, and their accounts were mostly exaggerated.

sentences.zh: 真宗一日以問慎修，對曰：「煜或懵理若此，何以享國十餘年？

translations.literal: One day Zhenzong questioned Shenxiu about this, who replied: "If Yu were truly so muddled in principle as this, how could he have kept his state for more than ten years?
translations.idiomatic: One day Emperor Zhenzong asked Shenxiu about this. Shenxiu replied, "If Yu were truly as muddled as they say, how could he have held his realm for more than ten years?

sentences.zh: 」他日，對宰相語及之，且言慎修溫雅不忘本，得臣子之操，深嘉獎之。

translations.literal: " Another day, speaking to the chief ministers he mentioned it, and moreover said Shenxiu was warm and refined and did not forget his origins, attained the conduct of minister and subject, and deeply praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: " On another day, speaking with his chief ministers, the emperor related this and praised Shenxiu for his warm refinement and loyalty to his roots, saying he embodied the conduct proper to a minister—and deeply commended him.

sentences.zh: 當時士大夫與之遊者，咸推其素尚。

translations.literal: At the time scholars and officials who traveled and associated with him all praised his lifelong aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials who associated with him at the time all admired his steadfast character.

sentences.zh: 然頗恃前輩，待後進倨慢，人以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he somewhat relied on being senior, treated juniors with haughty slowness, and people for this slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he leaned heavily on his seniority and treated juniors with cold arrogance; for this people held him somewhat cheap.

sentences.zh: 有集五卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in five juan.

sentences.zh: 汝士至工部員外郎，直集賢院。

translations.literal: Rushi rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and served directly in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi eventually became vice director of the Ministry of Works and served on direct staff at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 杜鎬，字文周，常州無錫人。

translations.literal: Du Gao, style name Wenchou, was a native of Wuxi in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gao, courtesy name Wenchou, was from Wuxi in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父昌業，南唐虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Changye was Vice Director of the Ministry of Works of Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Changye served Southern Tang as vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 鎬幼好學，博貫經史。

translations.literal: Gao from youth loved learning and broadly mastered the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gao loved learning and mastered the classics and histories with broad thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 兄為法官，嘗有子毀父畫像，為旁親所訟，疑其法不能決。

translations.literal: His elder brother was a legal officer; once a son destroyed his father's portrait painting, was sued by collateral kin, and his brother doubted the law and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother served as a legal officer. Once a son defaced his father's portrait and was sued by kinsmen; his brother found the case unclear under existing law and could not decide it.

sentences.zh: 鎬曰：「僧道毀天尊、佛像，可比也。

translations.literal: Gao said: "When monks and Daoists destroy images of the Heavenly Worthy and Buddha, it may be compared.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "When monks and Daoists deface images of the Heavenly Worthy or the Buddha, the offense is comparable.

sentences.zh: 」兄甚奇之。

translations.literal: " His elder brother was greatly struck by this.
translations.idiomatic: " His elder brother was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，解褐集賢校理，入直澄心堂。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination, upon leaving office dress became collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and entered direct duty at the Hall of Clear Hearts.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the mingjing examination, he entered service as collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and served on direct duty at the Hall of Clear Hearts.

sentences.zh: 江南平，授千乘縣主簿。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he was appointed chief clerk of Qiansheng County.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified, he was appointed chief clerk of Qiansheng County.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，江左舊儒多薦其能，改國子監丞、崇文院檢討。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, old scholars of the left Jiang region mostly recommended his ability; he was changed to deputy director of the Directorate of Education and collator of the Court of Sacred Writings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong acceded, many former Jiangnan scholars recommended his talents, and he was appointed deputy director of the Directorate of Education and collator at the Court of Sacred Writings.

sentences.zh: 會將祀南郊，彗星見，宰相趙普召鎬問之。

translations.literal: It happened that they were about to sacrifice at the Southern Suburban Altar; a comet appeared, and Chief Minister Zhao Pu summoned Gao to question him.
translations.idiomatic: As preparations were underway for a sacrifice at the Southern Suburban Altar, a comet appeared. Chief Minister Zhao Pu summoned Gao to consult him.

sentences.zh: 鎬曰：「當祭而日食，猶廢；

translations.literal: Gao said: "When sacrifice is due and there is a solar eclipse, it is still abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "When a sacrifice is scheduled and a solar eclipse occurs, the rite is still abandoned;

sentences.zh: 況謫見如此乎？

translations.literal: How much more when a banished star appears thus?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when a banished star appears like this?

sentences.zh: 」普言於上，即罷其禮。

translations.literal: " Pu spoke to the emperor, and immediately the rite was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: " Pu reported this to the emperor, and the ceremony was canceled at once.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遷著作佐郎，改太子左贊善大夫，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: The next day he was transferred to assistant compiler, changed to Grand Master of Left Admonition of the Heir Apparent, and granted crimson robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was promoted to assistant compiler, then made grand master of left admonition for the heir apparent and granted the crimson robe and fish tally of rank.

sentences.zh: 歷殿中丞、國子博士，加秘閣校理。

translations.literal: He passed through palace censor and erudite of the Directorate of Education, and was added as collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He served as palace censor and erudite of the Directorate of Education, and was additionally appointed collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 太宗觀書秘閣，詢鎬經義，進對稱旨，即日改虞部員外郎，加賜金帛。

translations.literal: Taizong viewed books in the Secret Archive, questioned Gao on the meaning of the classics; his advance and reply matched the emperor's intention, and that same day he was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, with additional gifts of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong reviewed books in the Secret Archive and questioned Gao on the classics, Gao's answers pleased him; that same day Gao was made vice director of the Ministry of Works and given additional gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 又問：「西漢賜與悉用黃金，而近代為難得之貨，何也？

translations.literal: He also asked: "In Western Han bestowals all used yellow gold, yet in recent times it is a hard-to-obtain treasure—why?
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "In Western Han, imperial gifts were all paid in gold—why has gold become so scarce in recent times?

sentences.zh: 」鎬曰：「當是時，佛事未興，故金價甚賤。

translations.literal: " Gao said: "At that time, Buddhist affairs had not risen, so the price of gold was very cheap.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao replied, "In that era Buddhist institutions had not yet proliferated, so gold was very cheap.

sentences.zh: 」又嘗召問天寶梨園事，敷奏詳悉。

translations.literal: " He was again summoned and questioned on affairs of the Pear Garden in the Tianbao reign; his exposition and report were detailed and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: " On another occasion the emperor questioned him about the Pear Garden entertainments of the Tianbao era, and Gao answered with exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 再遷駕部員外郎，判太常禮院，與朱昂、劉承珪編次館閣書籍，虞部郎中，事畢，賜金紫，改直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, judged at the Court of Ritual of the Grand Steward, together with Zhu Ang and Liu Chenggui arranged and ordered library pavilion books, became Director of the Ministry of Works; when the task was finished he was granted gold seal and purple robe, and changed to direct duty at the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice director of the Ministry of Rites and assigned to the Court of Ritual of the Grand Steward; together with Zhu Ang and Liu Chenggui he catalogued the palace library collections, then rose to director of the Ministry of Works. When the work was complete he was granted gold seal and purple robe and appointed to direct duty at the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 會修《太祖實錄》，命鎬檢討故事，以備訪問。

translations.literal: When they compiled the Veritable Records of Taizu, Gao was ordered to investigate and collate precedents to prepare for inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: During the compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu, Gao was charged with investigating historical precedents for reference.

sentences.zh: 景德初，置龍圖閣待制，因以命錫鎬，加都官郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde the Dragon Diagram Pavilion Attendant Academician was established, and accordingly this appointment was bestowed on Gao, who was additionally made Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingde era the post of attendant academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion was created, and Gao received the appointment along with promotion to director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 從幸澶淵，遇懿德皇后忌日，疑軍中鼓吹之禮，時鎬先還備儀仗，命馳騎問之。

translations.literal: Following the emperor's visit to Chanyuan, they encountered the anniversary of Empress Yide's death and doubted the ritual of drums and pipes in the army; at the time Gao had returned first to prepare ceremonial guard, and the emperor ordered a fast rider to ask him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Chanyuan, the anniversary of Empress Yide's death fell during the campaign, raising doubts about military music and fanfare. Gao had already returned ahead to prepare the ceremonial guard, and the emperor sent a fast rider to consult him.

sentences.zh: 鎬以武王載木主伐紂，前歌後舞為對。

translations.literal: Gao replied with King Wu carrying the wooden spirit tablet to smite Zhou, singing before and dancing behind.
translations.idiomatic: Gao answered by citing King Wu, who marched against Zhou while carrying the spirit tablet of his father—singing in front and dancing behind.

sentences.zh: 預修《冊府元龜》，改司封郎中。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Treasury and was changed to Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Treasury and was transferred to director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜右諫議大夫、龍圖閣直學士，賜襲衣、金帶，班在樞密直學士下。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Master, Academician Direct of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, granted ceremonial robe and gold belt, his court rank below direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made right remonstrating grand master and direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, granted ceremonial robe and gold belt, with court rank below the direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時特置此職，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: At the time this post was specially established, and Confucian scholars honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Because this post had been created especially for scholars, men of learning took it as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，同詳定東封儀注，遷給事中。

translations.literal: During Dazhong Xiangfu he jointly worked out in detail the ritual protocols for the eastern feng sacrifice and was transferred to Chief Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era he helped determine the ritual protocols for the eastern feng sacrifice and was promoted to chief gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，又置本閣學士，遷鎬工部侍郎，充其職。

translations.literal: In the third year the academicians of this pavilion were again established; Gao was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and filled that post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Dragon Diagram Pavilion's academicians were established anew; Gao was promoted to vice minister of works and appointed to that post.

sentences.zh: 上日，賜宴秘閣，上作詩賜之，進秩禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: On the day of appointment he was granted a banquet at the Secret Archive; the emperor composed a poem and bestowed it, and he was advanced in rank to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his appointment the emperor hosted a banquet in the Secret Archive, composed a poem in his honor, and promoted him to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, winter, he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the sixth year, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 錄其子渥為大理寺丞及三孫官。

translations.literal: His son Wo was enrolled as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, and three grandsons were given offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wo was appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, and three grandsons were given government posts.

sentences.zh: 鎬博聞強記，凡所檢閱，必戒書吏云：「某事，某書在某卷、幾行。

translations.literal: Gao had broad learning and a powerful memory; whenever he examined texts he always admonished the clerks, saying: "Such-and-such matter—such-and-such book is in such-and-such juan, such-and-such line.
translations.idiomatic: Gao possessed vast learning and a formidable memory. Whenever he reviewed texts he would tell the clerks exactly where to find a passage: "Such-and-such matter is in such-and-such book, juan such-and-such, line such-and-such."

sentences.zh: 」覆之，一無差誤。

translations.literal: " When checked, there was not one error.
translations.idiomatic: " When checked, not a single reference failed to match.

sentences.zh: 每得異書，多召問之，鎬必手疏本末以聞，顧遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Whenever rare books were obtained they often summoned him to question him; Gao always by hand wrote out origin and end to report, and imperial favor toward him was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the palace acquired a rare book the emperor would summon Gao; Gao would always write out by hand a full account of its provenance and content. The emperor favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 士大夫有所著撰，多訪以古事，雖晚輩、卑品請益，應答無倦。

translations.literal: Scholars and officials who had writings often inquired of him about ancient affairs; even juniors of low rank who sought instruction—he answered without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars with writings often consulted him on antiquities, and even juniors of humble rank who came seeking instruction never found him weary of answering.

sentences.zh: 年逾五十，猶日治經史數十卷，或寓直館中，四鼓則起誦《春秋》。

translations.literal: Past fifty years of age he still daily studied several tens of juan of classics and histories; sometimes lodging on direct duty in the academy, at the fourth watch he rose to recite the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Even after fifty he still read dozens of juan of classics and histories each day. When lodging on duty at the academy he would rise at the fourth watch to recite the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 所居僻陋，僅庇風雨，處之二十載，不遷徙。

translations.literal: His dwelling was remote and shabby, barely sheltering from wind and rain; he dwelled there twenty years without moving.
translations.idiomatic: His home was remote and mean, barely sheltering him from wind and rain; yet he lived there twenty years without moving.

sentences.zh: 燕居暇日，多挈醪饌以待賓友。

translations.literal: On leisurely days at home he often brought wine and food to await guests and friends.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure at home he often set out wine and dishes to welcome friends.

sentences.zh: 性和易，清素有懿行，士類推重之。

translations.literal: His nature was easygoing, his conduct pure and frugal with virtuous conduct; scholars esteemed and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Easygoing by nature and frugal in living, he was known for upright conduct, and men of learning held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 查道，字湛然，歙州休寧人。

translations.literal: Cha Dao, style name Zhanran, was a native of Xiuning in She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cha Dao, courtesy name Zhanran, was from Xiuning in She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖文徽，仕南唐至工部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wenhui served Southern Tang up to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wenhui served Southern Tang, rising to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 父元方，亦仕李煜，為建州觀察判官。

translations.literal: His father Yuanfang also served Li Yu as administrative aide to the observation commissioner of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanfang also served Li Yu as administrative aide to the Jianzhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王師平金陵，盧絳據歙州，遣使傳檄至郡，元方斬其使。

translations.literal: When the imperial army pacified Jinling, Lu Jiang held She Prefecture; he sent an envoy bearing a proclamation to the commandery, and Yuanfang beheaded the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army pacified Jinling, Lu Jiang seized She Prefecture and sent an envoy with a summons to the region. Yuanfang had the envoy executed.

sentences.zh: 及絳擒，太祖聞元方所為，優獎之。

translations.literal: When Jiang was captured, Taizu heard of Yuanfang's actions and generously rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang was captured, Emperor Taizu learned what Yuanfang had done and praised and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 拜殿中侍御史、知泉州，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed palace attendant censor and prefect of Quan Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed palace attendant censor and prefect of Quanzhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 道幼沉嶷不群，罕言笑，喜親筆硯，文徽特愛之。

translations.literal: Dao from youth was deep and lofty, not of the common herd, rarely speaking or laughing, loved to draw near brush and inkstone; Wenhui especially cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Dao was grave and uncommon, rarely laughing or speaking lightly, and loved to take up brush and ink. Wenhui doted on him especially.

sentences.zh: 未冠，以詞業稱。

translations.literal: Before cap and girdle he was famed for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he was already known for his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 侍母渡江，奉養以孝聞。

translations.literal: He attended his mother across the Yangtze and was heard of for supporting and nourishing her with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied his mother across the Yangtze and became known for devoted filial care.

sentences.zh: 母嘗病，思鱖羹，方冬苦寒，市之不獲。

translations.literal: His mother once fell ill and craved mandarin-fish soup; it was winter and bitterly cold, and it could not be obtained in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill she craved mandarin-fish soup; it was deep winter and bitter cold, and none could be found in the markets.

sentences.zh: 道泣禱於河，鑿冰取之，得鱖尺許以饋。

translations.literal: Dao wept and prayed at the river, broke the ice and took fish, obtaining a mandarin fish about a foot long to offer as food.
translations.idiomatic: Dao wept and prayed by the river, broke through the ice, caught a fish about a foot long, and presented it to her.

sentences.zh: 又刲臂血寫佛經，母疾尋愈。

translations.literal: He also cut his arm and with the blood wrote a Buddhist sutra; his mother's illness soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut his arm and copied a Buddhist sutra in his own blood; soon his mother recovered.

sentences.zh: 後數年，母卒，絕意名宦，遊五臺，將落發為僧。

translations.literal: Several years later his mother died; he cut off all intent for fame and office, traveled to Wutai, and was about to shave the head and become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later, after his mother's death, he renounced all ambition for office, traveled to Mount Wutai, and prepared to take vows as a monk.

sentences.zh: 一夕，震雷破柱，道坐其下，了無怖色，寺僧異之，咸勸以仕。

translations.literal: One night thunder split a pillar; Dao sat beneath it with utterly no look of fear; the temple monks marveled at him and all urged him to take office.
translations.idiomatic: One night thunder split a pillar while Dao sat beneath it without the slightest sign of fear. The monks marvelled and all urged him to enter official life.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，舉進士高第，解褐館陶尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he passed the jinshi examination in the top grade, and upon leaving office dress became magistrate of Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Duangong era he passed the jinshi examination with high marks and entered service as magistrate of Guantao.

sentences.zh: 曹彬鎮徐州，辟為從事，深被禮遇。
