translations.literal: Cao Bin governed Xuzhou and recruited him as staff officer; he was deeply treated with courtesy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin governed Xuzhou he recruited Dao as a staff officer and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 改興元觀察推官。

translations.literal: He was changed to administrative aide of the Xingyuan observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrative aide under the Xingyuan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寇準薦其才，授著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun recommended his talent, and he was appointed assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun recommended his abilities, and he was appointed assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，蜀寇叛，命道通判遂州。

translations.literal: During Chunhua Shu bandits rebelled; Dao was ordered as vice prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era, when bandits rebelled in Shu, Dao was appointed vice prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 召對，出御書曆，俾錄其課，給以實奉。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, the emperor produced an imperial calendar and ordered him to record his performance evaluations, granting him actual salary.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, the emperor presented him with an imperial calendar, instructing him to record his performance evaluations and granting him full salary.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，有使兩川者，得道公正清潔之狀以聞，優詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao an envoy to the Two Chuan region reported Dao's record of integrity, fairness, purity, and incorruptibility to the court; an excellent edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhidao era an envoy to the Two Chuan reported on Dao's integrity and incorruptibility; the emperor issued a warm commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞，俄徙知果州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary and soon moved to serve as prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary and soon appointed prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 時寇黨尚有伏岩谷依險為柵者，其酋何彥忠集其徒二百餘，止西充之大木槽，彀弓露刃。

translations.literal: At the time bandit factions still lurked in rocky valleys and gorges, relying on perilous terrain to build palisades; their chieftain He Yanzhong gathered more than two hundred of his followers, halted at Damucao in Xichong, strung bows and bared blades.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits still lurked in mountain ravines, holding fortified positions in difficult terrain. Their leader He Yanzhong gathered more than two hundred followers at Damucao in Xichong, bows strung and blades bared.

sentences.zh: 詔書招諭之，未下，咸請發兵殄之。

translations.literal: An imperial edict was to summon and instruct them, but before it was issued all requested sending troops to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict of clemency was being prepared, but before it could be issued everyone urged sending troops to exterminate the bandits.

sentences.zh: 道曰：「彼愚人也，以懼罪，欲延命須臾爾。

translations.literal: Dao said: "They are foolish men; out of fear of crime they wish only to prolong life for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "They are foolish men who, fearing punishment, only wish to prolong their lives a little longer.

sentences.zh: 其黨豈無詿誤邪？

translations.literal: Among their band how could there not be those misled in error?
translations.idiomatic: Surely not every man among them is truly guilty?

sentences.zh: 」遂微服單馬數僕，不持尺刃，間關林壑百里許，直趨賊所。

translations.literal: " Thereupon in plain dress, alone on horseback with a few servants, carrying not even a foot-long blade, he traversed a hundred li through forests and ravines with difficulty, going straight toward the bandits' place.
translations.idiomatic: " Then, dressed plainly, he rode alone with only a few servants, carrying no weapon, and traveled a hundred li through forested ravines straight to the bandits' camp.

sentences.zh: 初悉驚畏，持滿外向。

translations.literal: At first all were startled and fearful, holding bows drawn and facing outward.
translations.idiomatic: At first they were all alarmed, bows drawn and aimed outward.

sentences.zh: 道神色自若，踞胡床而坐，諭以詔意。

translations.literal: Dao's expression was as if at ease; he sat astride a camp chair and instructed them in the meaning of the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Dao remained perfectly composed, sat on a folding camp chair, and explained the emperor's amnesty.

sentences.zh: 或識之曰：「郡守也，嘗聞其仁，是寧害我者。

translations.literal: Someone who recognized him said: "It is the prefect; I have heard he is benevolent—he would not harm us.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recognized him and said, "This is the prefect. I've heard he is humane—he would never harm us.

sentences.zh: 」即相率投順羅拜，號呼請罪，悉給券歸農。

translations.literal: " Immediately they led one another in turning to allegiance, bowed in circles, cried out begging forgiveness; all were given certificates and sent back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: " At once they submitted in succession, prostrating themselves and begging forgiveness. Dao issued certificates to all and sent them back to farming.

sentences.zh: 加賜袍帶驛奏，璽書褒諭。

translations.literal: He was additionally granted robe, belt, and relay-horse memorial privilege; an imperial seal letter praised and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: The court additionally granted him robe, belt, and relay-horse privileges for memorials; an imperial sealed letter praised his achievement.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年代歸，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping his term ended and he returned; he was granted crimson robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping his term expired and he returned to court, receiving the crimson robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 上言曰：「朝廷命轉運使、副，不惟審度金穀，蓋以察廉郡縣，庶臻治平，以召和氣。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "When the court appoints transport commissioners and their deputies, it is not only to examine and measure gold and grain, but also to inspect and test integrity in commanderies and counties, hoping to reach ordered peace and thereby summon harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "When the court appoints transport commissioners and their deputies, the aim is not only to audit revenue and grain, but also to inspect the integrity of prefectures and counties—so that good governance may prevail and harmony flourish.

sentences.zh: 今觀所至，或匪盡公，蓋無懲勸之科，致有因循之弊。

translations.literal: Now observing where they arrive, some are not entirely fair—probably because there are no standards for punishment and encouragement, leading to the ill of dragging on perfunctorily.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commissioners now on tour are not always impartial, largely because there are no clear rewards and punishments, which breeds laxity and neglect.

sentences.zh: 望自今每使回日，先令具任內曾薦舉才識者若干，奏絀貪猥者若干，朝廷議其否臧，以為賞罰。

translations.literal: I hope that from now on, whenever each commissioner returns, he should first be ordered to list how many men of talent and discernment he recommended during his term and how many he reported as greedy and base; the court should deliberate their approval and disapproval, and use this for reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when each commissioner returns, require him first to report how many capable men he recommended and how many corrupt officials he impeached; let the court judge these accounts and reward or punish accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 俄出知寧州。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to serve as prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 會舉賢良方正之士，李宗諤以道名聞，策入第四等，拜左正言、直史館。

translations.literal: When worthy and upright scholars were recommended, Li Zong'e reported Dao's fame; his policy essay placed in the fourth rank, and he was appointed Left Corrective Speaker with direct duty at the Historiography Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During a recruitment of worthy and upright scholars, Li Zong'e nominated Dao, whose policy essay placed in the fourth rank. Dao was appointed left corrective speaker with direct duty at the Historiography Academy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為西京轉運副使。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as deputy transport commissioner of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed deputy transport commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 六年，始令三司使分部置副，召入，拜工部員外郎、充度支副使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year deputies were for the first time established at subdivisions under the Three Departments commissioner; he was summoned in, appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and deputy fiscal commissioner, granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the court first established deputy commissioners under subdivisions of the Three Departments. Dao was summoned back, appointed vice director of the Ministry of Works and deputy fiscal commissioner, and granted gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 道儒雅迂緩，治劇非所長。

translations.literal: Dao was refined and scholarly, dilatory and slow; governing urgent affairs was not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was scholarly and deliberate—managing urgent affairs was not his strength.

sentences.zh: 卞袞為鹽鐵副使，與道同候對，將升殿，遽出奏牘請道同署。

translations.literal: Bian Gun was deputy salt-and-iron commissioner; together with Dao he awaited audience; about to ascend the hall, he suddenly produced a memorial draft and asked Dao to co-sign.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Gun, deputy salt-and-iron commissioner, was waiting with Dao for audience. Just before entering the hall Bian suddenly produced a memorial and asked Dao to co-sign it.

sentences.zh: 及上詢問事本，道素未省視，不能對，遂以本官罷，出知襄州。

translations.literal: When the emperor inquired about the substance of the matter, Dao had never examined it and could not reply; he was therefore dismissed at his original rank and went out as prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor questioned him about the matter, Dao—who had never read the document—could not answer. He was removed from his post and appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒不能自辯，亦無慍色。

translations.literal: To the end he could not vindicate himself, yet showed no anger.
translations.idiomatic: He never offered a defense, yet showed not the least sign of resentment.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，歸直史館，遷刑部員外郎，預修《冊府元龜》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he returned to direct duty at the Historiography Academy, was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, and participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he returned to direct duty at the Historiography Academy, was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Justice, and took part in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Treasury.

sentences.zh: 三年，進秩兵部，為龍圖閣待制，與張知白、孫奭、王曙並命焉。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced in rank to the Ministry of War, made Attendant Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and appointed together with Zhang Zhibai, Sun Shi, and Wang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to the Ministry of War and appointed attendant academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, along with Zhang Zhibai, Sun Shi, and Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 加刑部郎中、判吏部選事，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Director of the Ministry of Justice, judged selection affairs at the Ministry of Personnel, and investigated and inspected capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made director of the Ministry of Justice, assigned to oversee personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel, and charged with inspecting capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，以久次，進右司郎中。

translations.literal: Sent on embassy to the Khitan; through long tenure he was advanced to Director of the Right Division.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as envoy to the Khitan, he was promoted to director of the right division on account of long service.

sentences.zh: 真宗退朝之暇，召馮元講《易》便坐，惟道與李虛己、李行簡預焉。

translations.literal: In his leisure after court when Zhenzong withdrew, he summoned Feng Yuan to lecture on the Book of Changes at the informal seat; only Dao, with Li Xuji and Li Xingjian, were among those present.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong had leisure after court, he summoned Feng Yuan to lecture on the Changes at the informal seat; Dao alone, with Li Xuji and Li Xingjian, was admitted.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，以耳聵難於對問，表求外任，得知虢州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, because deafness made answer in audience difficult, he memorialized requesting an outer post and was made prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi, finding his deafness made court audiences difficult, he petitioned for an outside appointment and was made prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 將行，上御龍圖閣飲餞之。

translations.literal: About to depart, the emperor went to the Dragon Diagram Pavilion to feast and send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure the emperor entertained him with a farewell feast at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 秋，蝗災民歉，道不候報，出官廩米賑之，又設粥糜以救饑者，給州麥四千斛為種於民，民賴以濟，所全活萬餘人。

translations.literal: In autumn, locust disaster made the people scarce in harvest; Dao did not await reports but released government granary rice to relieve them; he also set out gruel congee to rescue the hungry; he gave the prefecture's four thousand hu of wheat as seed to the people; the people relied on this to be delivered; those wholly kept alive numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a locust plague left the people short of grain. Dao, without waiting for authorization, issued government store rice for relief, set up gruel kitchens for the starving, and distributed four thousand hu of prefectural wheat as seed. More than ten thousand lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，卒，訃聞，真宗軫惜之。

translations.literal: In the second year, fifth month, he died; when the death report arrived, Zhenzong was deeply grieved and cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he died; when word reached court, Emperor Zhenzong grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 詔其子奉禮郎循之乘傳往治喪事，遷大理評事，賦祿終制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Xunzhi, Chamberlain for Ritual, to take relay horses and go to conduct funeral affairs; he was transferred to Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, with salary granted through mourning completion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his son Xunzhi, a chamberlain for ritual, to travel by relay horse to oversee the funeral, promoted him to evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, and granted salary through the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 道性淳厚，有犯不較，所至務寬恕，胥吏有過未嘗笞罰，民訟逋負者，或出己錢償之，以是頗不治。

translations.literal: Dao's nature was pure and thick; when offended he did not calculate; wherever he arrived he strove for clemency and forgiveness; clerks who had faults were never flogged and punished; when commoners sued over arrears, sometimes he paid from his own money; because of this he was rather not good at governing.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was naturally mild and magnanimous, never retaliating when wronged. Everywhere he served he favored leniency: clerks who erred were never flogged, and he sometimes paid out of his own purse to settle citizens' debt suits—so his administration tended toward laxity.

sentences.zh: 嘗出按部，路側有佳棗，從者摘以獻，道即計直掛錢於樹而去。

translations.literal: Once on tour of inspection, beside the road were fine jujubes; attendants plucked and presented them; Dao immediately reckoned the price and hung money on the tree, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Once while touring his district he came upon fine jujubes beside the road. When attendants picked some as a gift, he calculated a fair price and hung the coins on the tree before leaving.

sentences.zh: 兒時嘗戲畫地為大第，曰：「此當分贍孤遺。

translations.literal: As a child he once playfully drew the ground as a great mansion, saying: "This shall be divided to support orphans and the bereft."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he once traced a great mansion in the dirt and said, "This is to be shared among orphans and the bereft."

sentences.zh: 」及居京師，家甚貧，多聚親族之煢獨者，祿賜所得，散施隨盡，不以屑意。

translations.literal: " When he dwelt in the capital his household was very poor, yet he gathered many solitary kin of his clan; salary and gifts received he scattered in giving as fast as they came, not minding it with a scrap of concern.
translations.idiomatic: " In the capital his household was desperately poor, yet he took in many bereft kinsmen. Salary and gifts he handed out as fast as they arrived, without a thought for himself.

sentences.zh: 與人交，情公切至，廢棄孤露者，待之愈厚，多所周給。

translations.literal: In associating with people his feeling was fair, ardent, and utmost; to the abandoned and exposed he showed even greater depth, giving widely in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he was wholly devoted; toward the abandoned and friendless he was still more generous, aiding them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 初，赴舉，貧不能上，親族裒錢三萬遺之。

translations.literal: At first, going to the examinations, he was too poor to attend; clansmen pooled thirty thousand cash and presented it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first set out for the civil examinations he was too poor to go; kinsmen pooled thirty thousand cash and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 道出滑臺，過父友呂翁家。

translations.literal: Dao passed out through Huatai and visited the home of his father's friend the old man Lü.
translations.idiomatic: On his way Dao passed through Huatai and called on his father's friend Old Master Lü.

sentences.zh: 翁喪，貧窶無以葬，其母兄將鬻女以襄事。

translations.literal: The old man had died; the family was destitute with nothing for burial; his mother's elder brother was about to sell a daughter to accomplish the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The old man had died, leaving the family too poor for burial; Lü's wife's elder brother meant to sell a daughter to pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 道傾褚中錢與之，且為其女擇婿，別加資遣。

translations.literal: Dao poured out all the money in his satchel and gave it, and also chose a son-in-law for the daughter, separately adding dowry for her departure.
translations.idiomatic: Dao emptied his purse for them, found a husband for the daughter, and added a separate dowry besides.

sentences.zh: 又故人卒，貧甚，質女婢於人。

translations.literal: Again an old acquaintance died, very poor, pledging a maidservant to someone.
translations.idiomatic: Another old friend died in such poverty that his family had pledged a maidservant as security.

sentences.zh: 道為贖之，嫁士族。

translations.literal: Dao ransomed her for him and married her into a scholar family.
translations.idiomatic: Dao redeemed the girl and married her into a gentry family.

sentences.zh: 搢紳服其履行。

translations.literal: Gentry and officials admired his conduct and practice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and gentry alike admired his conduct.

sentences.zh: 好學，嗜弈棋，深信內典。

translations.literal: He loved learning, was addicted to weiqi, and deeply believed in Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, was devoted to weiqi, and was a devoted student of Buddhist sutras.

sentences.zh: 平居多茹蔬，或止一食，默坐終日，服玩極於卑儉。

translations.literal: Ordinarily he mostly ate vegetables, sometimes stopping at one meal, sitting silently the whole day; clothing and ornaments were at the utmost of lowliness and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He lived chiefly on vegetables, sometimes taking only one meal a day, and would sit in silent meditation from dawn to dusk. His dress and possessions were almost absurdly plain.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢神人謂曰：「汝位至正郎，壽五十七。

translations.literal: Once he dreamed a divine man telling him: "Your rank will reach Director of the Proper, lifespan fifty-seven."
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed that a spirit told him, "You will rise to the rank of director in the proper bureau and live fifty-seven years."

sentences.zh: 」而享年六十四，論者以為積善所延也。

translations.literal: " Yet his years enjoyed reached sixty-four; commentators held it extension through accumulated goodness.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet he lived to sixty-four; later writers attributed the extra years to the merit he had stored up.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，從兄陶。

translations.literal: He had a collection in twenty juan. Cousin Tao.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection in twenty juan. His cousin Tao [follows].

sentences.zh: 從兄 陶

translations.literal: Cousin: Tao
translations.idiomatic: Cousin: Tao

sentences.zh: 陶，字大均，初事李煜，以明法登科，補常州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Tao, style name Dajun, at first served Li Yu; through clarity in law he passed the examination, was supplemented as recorder-assistant of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, courtesy name Dajun, first served Li Yu. He passed the examination in statutory law and was appointed recorder-assistant of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，詔大理評事，試律學，除本寺丞，遷大理正，歷侍御史、權判大理寺，賜緋。

translations.literal: Upon returning to the dynasty, by edict he was made Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review; he tested in statutory studies, was appointed director within that office, was transferred to Chief of Justice, and successively served as Attending Censor and acting judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and was granted crimson.
translations.idiomatic: After surrender to the Song he was made evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, examined in statutory studies, appointed director within the court, promoted to chief of the court, and served successively as attending censor and acting chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, receiving the crimson robe.

sentences.zh: 斷官仲禹錫訟陶用法非當，陶抗辯得雪。

translations.literal: The sentencing officer Zhong Yu prosecuted Tao for improper application of law in a case; Tao argued in defense and was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The sentencing officer Zhong Yu sued Tao for misapplying the statutes; Tao defended himself successfully and was exonerated.

sentences.zh: 遷工部郎中，俄知台州，累遷兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Works, soon made prefect of Tai Prefecture, and cumulatively transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Ministry of Works, soon appointed prefect of Taizhou, and eventually rose to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，朱博為大理，議趙文海罪不當，宰相請以陶代。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, Zhu Bo was Chief of the Court of Judicial Review; in deliberating Zhao Wenhai's offense he held the crime inappropriate; the chief minister requested to replace him with Tao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianping Zhu Bo headed the Court of Judicial Review and ruled Zhao Wenhai's offense improperly classified; the chief minister asked that Tao replace him.

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「聞陶亦深文，當加戒勖。

translations.literal: Zhenzong said: "I hear Tao also applies law with harsh elaboration; he should be admonished and exhorted."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said, "I hear Tao also applies the law harshly; he should be sternly warned."

sentences.zh: 」即遷秘書少監、判寺事。

translations.literal: " Immediately he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and acting chief of the court.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then appointed vice director of the Secretariat with acting charge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時楊億知審刑，陶屢攻其失，又命代之，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Yi was in charge of Reviewing Punishments; Tao repeatedly attacked his errors; again he was ordered to replace him, and was granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi then headed the Office of Reviewing Punishments; Tao repeatedly exposed his mistakes, was again ordered to replace him, and received gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 陶持法深刻，用刑多失中，前後坐罰金百餘斤，皆以失入，無誤出者。

translations.literal: Tao held the law with deep severity; in applying punishment he often missed the mean; before and after he was fined more than a hundred jin of gold—all from wrongful conviction, with none from wrongful release.
translations.idiomatic: Tao applied the law with pitiless severity and often overshot the mark. He was fined more than a hundred jin of gold on repeated occasions, always for convicting too harshly, never for letting the guilty go free.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde he died, age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Jingde, at seventy.

sentences.zh: 子：拱之，淳化三年進士，後為都官郎中；

translations.literal: Sons: Gongzhi, jinshi in the third year of Chunhua, later Director of the Office for Regulating Officials;
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Gongzhi, a jinshi of Chunhua 3, later director of the Office for Regulating Officials;

sentences.zh: 慶之，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Qingzhi, Middle Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: and Qingzhi, middle attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 論曰：典誥命者，以詞章典雅為先；

translations.literal: Commentary: For those who draft edicts and commands, elegant literary composition comes first;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: For drafters of edicts and commands, elegance of style comes first;

sentences.zh: 侍講讀者，以道德洽聞為貴。

translations.literal: for attendant lecturers and readers, moral virtue widely heard is esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: for palace lecturers and readers, moral authority widely respected is prized.

sentences.zh: 自昔皆難其人，至宋尤重其選。

translations.literal: From antiquity finding such men has been difficult; in Song the selection was especially weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the right men has always been difficult; the Song court valued the choice still more highly.

sentences.zh: 太宗崇尚儒術，聽政之暇，以觀書為樂，置翰林侍讀學士以備顧問。

translations.literal: Taizong honored Confucian technique; in leisure from hearing cases he took reading books as pleasure, establishing Hanlin Attendant Reader academicians to provide for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong esteemed Confucian learning; in leisure from governing he took books as his delight and established Hanlin attendant reader academicians as his advisors.

sentences.zh: 真宗克紹先誌，兼置侍講學士，且因內閣以設職名，俾鴻碩之士更直迭宿，相與從容講論。

translations.literal: Zhenzong was able to continue the former plan, additionally establishing Attendant Lecturer academicians, and moreover using the inner bureau to set office titles, causing great scholars to rotate night watches in succession, mutually with ease discussing and debating.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong carried on his father's design, adding palace lecturer posts and drawing on the inner secretariat to define their titles, so that eminent scholars rotated night duty in turn for unhurried discussion and debate.

sentences.zh: 以丕之清介，頑之和豫，顥之明敏，茂直之淳厚，俾領詞職，固無忝矣。

translations.literal: With Pi's purity and integrity, Hang's harmony and ease, Hao's brilliance and quickness, and Maozhi's genuineness and depth, making them lead literary offices—truly they did not disgrace the post.
translations.idiomatic: Han Pi's integrity, Shi Hang's geniality, Liang Hao's brilliance, and Zhang Maozhi's steadfastness made them fit leaders of the literary offices without disgrace to the post.

sentences.zh: 若文仲之器韻淹雅，慎修之醞藉該貫，杜鎬之博聞強識，查道之純孝篤義，置諸左右，啟沃尤多，豈直講論文義而已哉。

translations.literal: If Wenzhong's instrument and tone are broad and refined, Shenxiu's cultured breadth and mastery, Gao's wide hearing and strong memory, and Dao's pure filial piety and steadfast righteousness are placed at left and right, nourishment and moistening are especially many—how would it be only lecturing and discussing literary meaning?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenzhong's cultivated grace, Pan Shenxiu's polished breadth, Du Gao's encyclopedic memory, and Cha Dao's filial devotion, set at the emperor's side, enriched counsel far beyond mere lectures on literary doctrine.

sentences.zh: 若祐之不喜趨競，徽之深疾幸進，風采凝峻，又其卓然者也。

translations.literal: As for Youzhi's dislike of scrambling competition, Huizhi's deep loathing of fawning advancement—their bearing stern and lofty—these too are among those who stand out.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youzhi's refusal to scramble for preferment and Yang Huizhi's revulsion at currying favor—their bearing grave and austere—marked them as still more exceptional.

sentences.zh: 徽之嘗謂：「溫仲舒、寇準以搏擊取貴位，使後輩務習趨競，禮俗浸薄。

translations.literal: Huizhi once declared: "Wen Zhongshu and Kou Zhun used aggressive attack to win exalted rank, causing later generations to devote themselves to scrambling competition, and ritual custom gradually grew thin."
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi once said, "Wen Zhongshu and Kou Zhun won high rank by bare-knuckle politics, teaching younger men to scramble for advancement until ritual and custom thinned away."

sentences.zh: 」君子以為名言云。

translations.literal: " Men of honor held this to be a saying of renown.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of honor judged it a remark worth heeding.
